title: A Genetic-Reinforcement Learning Algorithm Based Fuzzy Distributed Frequency Regulation Strategy With Virtual Power Plant Under PMU Missing Data
abstract: This paper investigates the frequency regulation problem on power system with virtual power plant (VPP) under phasor measurement unit (PMU) missing data. First, the distributed load frequency control (LFC) incorporating VPP is established, in which a unified dynamic model based on VPP is introduced with the consideration of PMU missing data. Then, a genetic-reinforcement learning algorithm is developed to optimize the power output of various frequency regulation resources. Furthermore, a fuzzy dynamic event-triggered mechanism (FDETM) is proposed to achieve the balance between bandwidth resource utilization and frequency regulation performance. Finally, theoretical analysis is conducted using Lyapunov theory. Sufficient conditions for ensuring the system stability are derived. Evaluations on IEEE 9-bus test system in MATLAB/Simulink and IEEE 39-bus test system on hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiment platform demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy.

title: Adaptive Liquid Time-Constant Equivalent Dynamic Model With Transfer Learning for Active Distribution Networks With Grid-Forming IBRs
abstract: Active distribution networks (ADNs) integrating grid-forming and grid-following inverter-based resources (IBRs) introduce complex dynamics and demand accurate, practical data-driven models for integrated transmission-distribution system analysis and control. Existing models, however, require extensive data and lack versatility across diverse ADN operating conditions and configurations. To address these limitations, this paper leverages recent advances in machine learning and presents a data-driven liquid-time-constant (LTC) equivalent dynamic model for ADNs. The LTC architecture enables an enhanced representation of the complex temporal dynamics of ADNs with IBRs, including their source and control dynamics. Further, the proposed model integrates transfer learning (TL) to enable knowledge transfer across operational scenarios and improve prediction robustness and accuracy in data-scarce, realistic ADNs. A modified version of the CIGRE ADN benchmark, interconnected with the WSCC 9-bus transmission system, is used for extensive comparative studies. Compared with long short-term memory, nonlinear autoregressive exogenous, and Kolmogorov–Arnold network models, the proposed model demonstrated robustness, accuracy, low latency, low memory consumption, and generalization across a wide range of operating conditions, particularly during severe disturbances such as short-circuit faults and under limited-data conditions. Furthermore, the proposed LTC model exhibited improved resilience under unseen disturbances, out-of-distribution operating scenarios, and variations in both system parameters and modeling assumptions. Moreover, testing on ADNs with different configurations, such as the CIGRE ADN and modified IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus ADNs, shows that the integrated LTC–TL framework provides superior cross-topology generalization, enabling effective knowledge transfer when fine-tuned using limited target-domain datasets from such heterogeneous benchmarks.

title: Multi-Frequency Injection-Based Wideband Signal Measurement Method and Its Application in Grid-Connected Inverter
abstract: Wideband impedance characteristics play an essential role in renewable energy grid-connected stability analysis, and multi-frequency injection based wideband signal measurement is an effective method to extract impedance characteristics quickly. However, due to the spectral leakage and low frequency resolution, existing measurement methods such as fast Fourier transform (FFT) suffer from poor measurement accuracy under multi-frequency conditions. To tackle this issue, a wideband measurement method is proposed to extract grid-inverter impedance characteristics from the time-domain perspective. First, the concept of deterministic components in impedance measurement is introduced, and the impedance measurement is regarded as deterministic components measurement. Then, a high-precision deterministic components measurement method is proposed. By approximating the fundamental frequency through a first polynomial fitting and then solving the deterministic components through a second polynomial fitting, the deterministic components can be accurately extracted in the presence of fundamental frequency deviation and noise. To validate the performance of the proposed method, simulations and actual measurement experiments are carried out. The results demonstrate that the impedance amplitude errors of the proposed method are less than 1.8 dB, and the phase errors are less than 5.5° under the test conditions, which are significantly lower than those of existing wideband measurement methods.

title: Condition-Driven Direct-to-Satellite Multi-UAV Inspection for Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: With the expansion of offshore wind farms, the complex maritime conditions and harsh offshore environments pose challenges to routine inspections, including limited communication connectivity and poor response timeliness. In this article, a condition-driven direct-to-satellite multi-UAV inspection scheme is proposed. Deviating from conventional geometry-based routing, a novel prioritization mechanism is developed to intrinsically couple the anomalous electrical states of offshore wind turbines (OWTs) with spatial flight geometries. The scheme further improves operational efficiency by optimizing UAV trajectories under a priority-consistent sensor wake-up mapping for minimum inspection time. However, the formulated optimization problem is inherently a nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) with an unknown number of time slots, which makes conventional methods ineffective. To overcome this challenge, the problem is reformulated as a Markov decision process (MDP), and a K-means pre-partitioned soft actor-critic (KP-SAC) algorithm is developed to efficiently search for high-quality solutions. Simulation results verify that the proposed method significantly reduces inspection completion time compared with the baseline schemes under diverse sensing-load settings and communication conditions. From an offshore wind farm operation perspective, the post-processing evaluation demonstrates that reduced inspection completion time enables earlier inspection-triggered intervention, with shorter periods of degraded operating conditions and curtailed available output.

title: Robust Energy Management of Hybrid Microgrids via a Nonintrusive Load Monitoring Framework With Dual-Task Learning
abstract: Nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) is a key technology for enhancing the demand-side flexibility of hybrid microgrid systems by enabling appliance-level consumption to be extrapolated from aggregated smart meter data without requiring dedicated sensors for each device. However, existing state-of-the-art NILM approaches based on deep learning neglect the environmental factors representing contextual drivers of energy consumption, and poorly balance the dual objectives of state classification and power estimation during model training. Moreover, existing robust energy management systems are unable to exploit available appliance-level information, particularly under conditions of high renewable energy source (RES) output uncertainties. The present work addresses these issues by proposing a dual-task NILM framework that performs appliance state detection and power consumption estimation jointly, while incorporating the electrical data in smart meters with contextual drivers of energy consumption, including environmental temperature, humidity, and solar radiation, in a multi-source data fusion design. The estimated appliance states and corresponding power consumption values are then embedded into a robust optimization framework for scheduling distributed resources and demand-side flexibility under RES output uncertainties. The superiority of the proposed NILM-based disaggregation and robust energy management approaches is demonstrated in comparison with state-of-the-art benchmark approaches based on the results of case studies using real-world data.

title: Fractional-Order Distributed Current Sharing Control for Power-Coupled Multi-Bus DC Microgrids: A Hierarchical Consensus Approach
abstract: Although the primary fractional-order PI controller, which can improve dynamic response features, has been widely applied in DC microgrids, the relative distributed secondary control has not been proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items and composite load generalized disturbances (including constant power/current loads). Thus, this paper introduces a fractional-order distributed secondary control (FODSC) strategy specifically designed for such multi-bus DC microgrids. Firstly, the standard fractional-order multi-agent state-space function model is built, including a primary fractional-order PI controller, a power coupling item, and so on. This standard model is an important foundation for hierarchical control design. Secondly, the state compensator is designed to solve the heterogeneous problem, which is caused by different energy resource rated capacity, RLC filter, and so on. Furthermore, the fractional-order distributed secondary control strategy is proposed to achieve accurate current sharing for multi-bus DC microgrids with power coupling items, effectively overcoming the negative damping effect induced by constant power loads. Meanwhile, the stability proof of the proposed control strategy is provided. Furthermore, a cyber-physical resilient mechanism is integrated to enable plug-and-play operations and system fault tolerance. Finally, simulation and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and practical implementability of the proposed strategy in achieving accurate current sharing.

title: Multi-Charging Station Pricing Strategy for Real-Time Congestion Management in Coupled Traffic-Power Networks
abstract: In high-density cities, coordinating charging station (CS) real-time pricing to mitigate traffic congestion is considered a promising approach. However, the increasing complexity of transportation systems and multi-player dynamic interactions limit the effectiveness of existing pricing strategies in real-time congestion management. To address these, a real-time coordinated pricing framework for multiple CSs in coupled traffic-power networks based on Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) simulation is proposed in this paper. First, based on the established CS selection model for EVs, SUMO is utilized to simulate the real-time vehicle and road conditions of the transportation system under given charging prices, providing feedback on charging demand as well as individual and global traffic congestion costs. Next, an Adversarial Diverse Ensemble (ADE) surrogate-based traffic state prediction model is developed to overcome the time-intensive nature of SUMO and integrate it into the multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework. Then, a Graph Attention Network-based bi-level multi-agent Soft Actor-Critic (GAT-BLMASAC) algorithm is proposed to solve the coordinated pricing problem in a bi-level architecture, where the upper level optimizes bidding strategies of generation companies (GenCos) as price-makers and the lower level coordinates pricing among CSs as price-takers. Finally, simulations on a real-world Hong Kong transport network demonstrate that the pricing strategies derived from the proposed framework significantly mitigate traffic congestion while enhancing the total profit of CSs. The proposed algorithm exhibits robust convergence in the multi-leader-multi-follower game, offering a scalable solution for coordinated CS pricing in high-density urban settings.

title: Trustworthy Reinforcement Learning for Renewable Base Energy Management Against Communication Failures
abstract: Renewable energy integration introduces volatility, posing significant challenges to power systems energy management. Conventional methods struggle to handle the volatility relying on high-fidelity models. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) offers an alternative by learning control policies based on environment interaction. However, communication failures and MW-scale renewable volatility cause delayed state perception and cascaded constraint violations, threatening both system reliability and economic efficiency, and limiting RL deployment. We formulate a communication-failure-tolerant DRL (CFT-DRL) framework that considers the grid-consistent belief state and physically operational envelopes simultaneously. A state belief estimation module is designed to alleviate state perception bias caused by communication failures. An operational-envelope-embedded mechanism is developed to incorporate operational envelopes into policy updates, complemented by a security execution layer to ensure strict constraint satisfaction. Considering the efficient learning and deployment feasibility, we align the policy exploration with physical state transitions. Comparative studies demonstrate superior robustness, operational feasibility, and readiness for practical deployment of the proposed method.

title: Two-Stage Active Distribution Network Voltage Control via LLM-RL Collaboration: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Approach
abstract: The growing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) into active distribution networks (ADNs) has exacerbated operational challenges, making it imperative to coordinate diverse equipment to mitigate voltage violations and enhance power quality. Although existing data-driven approaches have demonstrated effectiveness in the voltage control problem, they often require extensive trial-and-error exploration and struggle to incorporate heterogeneous information, such as day-ahead forecasts, semantic-based grid codes, and historical records. Considering the operational scenarios and requirements in real-world ADNs, in this paper, we propose a hybrid knowledge-data-driven approach that leverages dynamic collaboration between a large language model (LLM) agent and a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to achieve two-stage voltage control. In the day-ahead stage, the LLM agent receives coarse region-level forecasts and generates scheduling strategies for on-load tap changer (OLTC) and shunt capacitors (SCs) to regulate the overall voltage profile. Then in the intra-day stage, based on real-time node-level measurements, the RL agent refines terminal voltages by deriving reactive power generation strategies for PV inverters. On top of the LLM-RL collaboration framework, we further propose a self-evolution mechanism for the LLM agent and a pretrain-finetune pipeline for the RL agent, effectively enhancing and coordinating the policies for both agents. The proposed approach not only aligns more closely with practical operational characteristics but also effectively combines the complementary advantages of the LLM agent and the RL agent, significantly improving overall training efficiency and voltage control performance. Comprehensive comparisons and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Weather-Aware Feeder Fault Prediction Based on Graph Learning With Synthetic Rare Event Generation
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events have significantly challenged the reliability of power distribution systems. Accurate prediction of weather-related feeder fault states under such conditions is hindered by two fundamental issues: 1) the mismatch between the Euclidean assumptions of traditional machine learning and the inherently graph-structured nature of distribution feeders, and 2) the severe class imbalance caused by the rarity of weather-related fault data. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel framework that integrates a graph convolutional network (GCN) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). The proposed GCN-cGAN framework captures topological dependencies of feeders while synthesizing realistic rare fault events under extreme weather scenarios. A graph attention-based model is further developed for feeder fault prediction, leveraging both real and synthetic data samples. Extensive experiments on real distribution topology and meteorological data show consistent gains under multiple evaluation scenarios, including strong wind, heavy rainfall, and their combination, with marked robustness to class imbalance. Under the present prediction setting, compared with conventional and state-of-the-art baselines, Recall improves by about 28 percent and F1-score by about 21 percent.

title: Two-Stage Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Forecasting for Wind Generation With Defense Against Malicious Eavesdroppers and Saboteurs
abstract: Wind power generation point forecasting involves trade-offs among accuracy, privacy, attack resilience, and training efficiency. Individual forecasting (IF) protects data privacy but often suffers from limited accuracy, whereas collaborative forecasting (CF) exploits cross-farm correlations but may introduce privacy risks, malicious attacks, and high training costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient two-stage privacy-preserving CF framework. In Stage 1, each wind farm trains an IF model independently and in parallel. In Stage 2, all farms collaboratively train a collaborative fine-tuning (CFT) model to learn IF residuals, improving forecasting accuracy while reducing the collaborative training burden. Considering two types of malicious attackers in information interaction, namely eavesdroppers and saboteurs, targeted defense mechanisms are further designed. For eavesdroppers, secure multi-party computation is embedded into the CFT process, enabling both forward and backward propagation to be performed over secret shares and preventing privacy leakage. For saboteurs, dropout-embedded self-attention and quantile regression are incorporated to mitigate the impact of tampered collaborative information and constrain abnormal residual corrections. Case studies on real-world data from 10 wind farms in Jiangsu Province, China, and the public GEFCom2014 dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower collaborative training cost than federated-learning-based CF. Sensitivity analyses further reveal the effects of key defense-related parameters, providing practical guidance for parameter tuning under different security requirements.

title: An Economic Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Microgrid Distribution System Based on Bi-Level Flexibility Trading Mechanism
abstract: Coordinating distribution-local flexibility trading with multi-microgrid (MMG) scheduling offers an effective approach to managing distributed energy resources (DERs). However, existing scheduling strategies based on traditional flexibility trading mechanisms (FTMs) struggle to fully unlock the flexibility potential of DERs, leading to reduced overall economic efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes an economic scheduling strategy based on a new bi-level FTM for a multi-microgrid distribution system (MMDS). First, a bi-level FTM is designed. By peer-to-peer (P2P) and microgrid-to-distribution (M2D) flexibility trading, this bi-level FTM enables direct one-to-one flexibility transactions among all participants. On this basis, an economic scheduling strategy for MMG cooperation is proposed by fully considering flexibility regulation initiative and fair benefit allocation. Finally, case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively enhances resource utilization, economic performance, and stakeholder coordination within the MMDS.

title: On the Solvability of the Power Flow Equation of DC Microgrids Under Distributed Control Through an Infinite Union Method
abstract: For a DC microgrid with constant power loads (CPLs), the existence of feasible power flow solutions is a necessary condition for correct system operation, which is often challenging to solve. This paper analyzes the solvability of the power flow equation for a meshed DC microgrid, where some distributed generations (DGs) are under distributed consensus control (DCC-DGs) to achieve current sharing and voltage regulation, while other DGs are under MPPT control (MPPT-DGs). Firstly, the power flow equation of the DC microgrid is established. Secondly, for the solvability of the power flow equation, an infinite union method based on Brouwer’s fixed point theorem is proposed. Compared with existing results, the derived solvability condition provides a larger feasible region for the loads. Furthermore, the derived solvability condition not only guarantees the existence of power flow solutions but also allows for acceptable nodal voltage deviations and safe output currents. Finally, case studies validate the correctness of the proposed theorems.

title: Integrated Bayesian Inference for Online Inertia Estimation With Non Gaussian Posterior in Inverter Based Resources Interfaced Power Systems
abstract: In modern low inertia power systems with high inverter penetration, online inertia estimation has become challenging due to the presence of nonlinear converter control, virtual inertia loops, current saturation, measurement errors, and other practical uncertainties. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents an advanced Tree Pyramidal Adaptive Importance Sampling based Bayesian inference approach for the estimation of inertia and virtual inertia in an inverter-interfaced power system. Since the proposed algorithm possesses an adaptive proposal distribution refinement, it effectively explores the most probable parameter space. Hence, it reduces variance in inertia estimation results and converges early to the desired value of the inertia constant with fewer samples. The sample generation process is fully parallel, which supports faster execution. The proposed algorithm is robust against non-Gaussian posteriors that may arise due to non-linearity in the inertia estimation problem. The algorithm is hyperparameter-tuning-free and possesses an anytime property. The proposed algorithm is tested for inertia estimation in an IEEE 9 bus system interfaced with a PV-battery grid-following inverter for different scenarios of load shedding, load increment, weak and strong grids, non-Gaussian posterior, and Gaussian noise. Simulation and real-time results validate the superior performance of the proposed method for inertia estimation.

title: A Data-Driven Physics-Informed Defense Framework of DC Microgrids Against Cyberattacks
abstract: The increasing prevalence of DC microgrids (DCmGs) has exposed them to severe cybersecurity challenges, particularly false data injection (FDI) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. To address these threats, this paper proposes a data-driven physics-informed defense framework that efficiently integrates precise attack detection with smooth system recovery. At its core lies a physics-informed temporal generative adversarial network architecture (PiGAN). This model innovatively incorporates a linear attention mechanism to enhance temporal feature extraction. Simultaneously, it introduces physical constraints to ensure the reconstructed data strictly adhere to the intrinsic physical laws of DCmGs. To achieve accurate detection, an agent-based dynamic threshold detector is designed. This detector allows the system to adjust its anomaly sensitivity based on real-time operating conditions, thereby identifying dynamic and subtle attacks with high precision. Furthermore, to maintain system stability, a confidence-based smooth recovery strategy is developed. This strategy performs a dynamic weighted fusion of measured and reconstructed healthy data to enable a seamless transition from the attacked state to normal operation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an attack detection accuracy of up to 99.49%, effectively mitigating various malicious attacks and validating the framework’s efficiency and robustness.

title: In-situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography and multiphysics modeling of the failure mechanisms in an end-of-vehicle-life lithium-ion battery upon indentation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face safety and reliability challenges throughout service and retirement. However, the mechanistic relationships among mechanically induced structural damage, internal short-circuit (ISC) initiation, and subsequent thermal behavior remain insufficiently understood. This study presents an integrated experimental and computational framework for investigating structural evolution and ISC behavior in an 18,650 cylindrical cell subjected to quasi-static indentation. By integrating in-situ structural characterization with coupled multiphysics modeling, the framework correlates internal deformation and interfacial failure with ISC initiation and localized thermal responses. In-situ synchrotron X-ray micro- computed tomography and stepwise indentation enabled three-dimensional visualization of electrode deformation, layer interaction, and interfacial delamination in an end-of-life (EoL) cell. A finite element model examined the mechanical response and stress distribution of the multilayered cell architecture and identified failure-prone regions under spherical indentation. The model was calibrated against the measured mechanical response and observed deformation, providing a basis for subsequent mechanistic analysis. Building on the mechanically calibrated model, a coupled mechanical-electrochemical-thermal framework was established to clarify the progression from indentation-induced deformation to ISC initiation and subsequent heat generation at different states of charge. The results illustrate that enhanced ductility of the jellyroll components and improved interfacial cohesion can limit failure propagation across adjacent electrode and separator layers, thereby improving structural integrity and reducing ISC risk. Moreover, indentation-induced ISC can cause a pronounced localized temperature rise and heat accumulation even at 30% state of charge, indicating that the associated safety risk remains non-negligible even at low charge levels. The proposed framework provides experimentally grounded insight into mechanically induced battery failure and informs safer cell design, second-life applications, and recycling.

title: Agent-Based Pricing Strategy for Fast-Charging Stations Considering Price Responsiveness of Electric Vehicles at Large Scales
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) presents urgent demands for the efficient operation of fast-charging stations (FCSs), which must accommodate diverse user pReferences, high mobility, and spatiotemporal traffic variability. As these systems scale, one critical challenge lies in dynamically responding to the price-sensitive behavior of EV users under complex spatiotemporal conditions and pricing strategies. This paper proposes a data-driven, agent-based pricing framework for FCSs that captures both individual decision-making dynamics and collective behavior of EV fleets. Compared to conventional studies that rely on macroscopic traffic flow models (e.g., user equilibrium formulations) or regression-based charging load forecasts, this paper introduces a fine-grained, data-driven, agent-based pricing framework that captures both the microscopic decision-making dynamics of EVs and the emergent collective behaviors across large fleets. We first formulate a graph-embedded Markov Decision Process to simulate EV drivers’ route and charging choices, incorporating transportation and charging network features. A scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MA-DRL) algorithm with count-based abstraction is then proposed to jointly learn decentralized EV policies and enable collective coordination. To bridge behavioral modeling and demand forecasting, a deep Graph Attention Network (GAT) is trained to approximate the nonlinear, high-dimensional mapping between FCS attributes. Finally, an agent-based pricing model is designed to optimize FCS profits while accounting for users’ price sensitivity and electricity market constraints, with nodal prices obtained from a lower-level power distribution network optimization. Simulation results validate the framework’s effectiveness in modeling price-responsive EV charging behaviors and achieving economically efficient station operation under dynamic conditions.

title: Resilience Equity-Aware Distribution System and Energy Community Co-Planning With a Fair Subsidy Allocation Mechanism
abstract: Energy communities (ECs) are emerging as key actors in enhancing distribution system (DS) resilience. As the DS and multiple ECs participate in local planning and investment, a major challenge arises: how to coordinate their actions to ensure efficient and equitable access to resilience-enhancing resources across the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretic framework for joint resilience-enhancing planning of the DS with multiple ECs. The DS operator conducts grid expansion to facilitate the integration of distributed renewable energy sources (RESs). Concurrently, multiple ECs develop their distributed RES portfolios, optimizing for self-sufficiency while managing operational profitability uncertainties. Furthermore, resilience equity is defined as ensuring that all communities have equitable access to resilience services. Subsidies for distributed RES investment are allocated to ECs directly tied to their contribution to system resilience, with resilience equity serving as a fundamental factor in this assessment. Additionally, as exact Shapley value computation becomes intractable in large-scale systems, a stratified sampling approach is developed to achieve efficient and accurate approximations. Simulation studies on a modified European low-voltage test feeder demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing resilience while promoting resilience equity.

title: Grid-Aware Islanding and Resynchronisation of AC/DC Microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal, grid-aware supervisory control framework for the islanding, islanded operation, and resynchronisation of hybrid AC/DC microgrids. The framework relies on a unified hybrid AC/DC power flow (PF) model that explicitly represents the grid-forming operation of AC/DC interfacing converters (ICs). Sensitivity coefficients (SCs) are derived from this model and used to formulate the voltage and branch-current constraints of the optimal power flow (OPF). The considered operating mode is relevant for hybrid microgrids that aggregate DC-native or DC-interfaced resources, such as photovoltaic units, batteries, and electric vehicles, through a DC network. During islanded operation, the grid-forming IC regulates the AC voltage and frequency, while the active-power balance is supplied through the DC grid. This separates the active- and reactive-power slack locations and requires a dedicated PF and SC formulation. The proposed OPF computes the optimal setpoints that satisfy voltage and ampacity constraints before, during, and after the islanding manoeuvre, while local converter controls ensure voltage and frequency regulation in real time. The proposed framework is experimentally validated on a 27-node hybrid AC/DC network with three ICs and a mix of controllable and stochastic resources.

title: Output-to-Application Error Propagation in Neural Network-Based State Estimators for LV Grids
abstract: State estimation in low-voltage distribution grids is challenging due to limited measurement availability, unbalanced operation, and computational burden. While recent neural network-based estimators report high accuracy in voltage magnitude estimation, their reliability for downstream applications remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a multi-task neural network framework for estimating phase-to-ground voltage phasors in three-phase four-wire European-type unbalanced low-voltage grids using limited measurements. The reliability of such models is investigated not only in terms of the accuracy of predicted state variables but also in terms of the impact of estimation errors on derived electrical quantities. The results show that even small voltage estimation errors can lead to significant inaccuracies in derived power. Building on this insight, the neural network outputs are leveraged within a hybrid framework to initialize a conventional estimator, significantly reducing convergence time without compromising its accuracy. The findings reveal that accurate primary outputs do not necessarily guarantee reliable derived results, underscoring the need for evaluation strategies tailored to application-level requirements and the specific needs of each DSO. The article also addresses the question of whether models based exclusively on neural networks for this type of application can be considered complete state estimators or merely tools capable of providing acceptable estimates of certain electrical variables.

title: Model Predictive Black Start for Dynamic Formation of DER-Led Microgrids With Inrush Current Impacts
abstract: Black start (BS) of the distribution system (DS) with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) requires advanced control frameworks to ensure secure and efficient restoration. This paper proposes a model predictive black start (MPBS) framework that captures the mutual interaction between switching decisions and physical feasibility to generate restoration sequences. Short-term forecasts of DER output, load demand, and transmission grid (TG) availability are incorporated within a receding-horizon control structure to construct cranking paths. To evaluate decision-dependent feasibility, an analytical inrush current estimation method is developed based on dynamically formed microgrid (MG) nodal impedance matrices under worst-case (WC) switching conditions. To mitigate excessive inrush current and prevent protection misoperations, a structural preventive mechanism is introduced, combining an emergency operation–inspired voltage reduction strategy with a switch-blocking function executed in a hierarchical manner. The proposed inrush model is validated against electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations in PowerFactory with estimation accuracies exceeding 90%. Case studies on IEEE and EPRI networks demonstrate that the proposed MPBS framework effectively prevents fuse and recloser misoperations, reduces DER energy consumption, and improves load restoration efficiency during DER-led BS processes.

title: Vulnerability Analysis of Multi-Timescale DC Microgrids Under False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a vulnerability analysis for the multi-timescale DC microgrid (DCmG) against false data injection (FDI) attacks. Using singular perturbation theory, the system dynamics are decomposed into a fast boundary layer subsystem and a slow reduced-order model. Sufficient stability conditions for both subsystems are derived, and input-to-state stability (ISS) of the slow subsystem is established under attacks. Furthermore, a zonotopic reachability analysis is performed to estimate the worst-case state deviation and compute an analytical admissible attack indicator for safety assessment. Theoretical predictions are validated through both numerical simulations and full-hardware experiments. It is demonstrated that the multi-timescale property leads to new attack surfaces, and the analytical attack bounds are consistent with observed voltage deviations, which can effectively guide safe and secure control under cyber threats.

title: Adaptive Inertia of DC-Link Voltage Synchronization
abstract: DC-link voltage synchronization (DCVS) can be the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy for grid-forming converter, but its virtual inertia configuration problem remains unsolved. Therefore, this paper proposes a universal adaptive virtual inertia strategy for DCVS. The desired virtual inertia adaptively decreases with the rise of DC-link voltage deviation (frequency deviation), which is entirely opposite to that of the traditional VSG ignoring DC-link voltage dynamic. To configure the desired adaptive virtual inertia, the AC frequency of the interfaced inverter is correlated with the energy stored in DC-link capacitor by the linear proportional and power-law logic. It can effectively alleviate the trade-off problem between DC-link voltage fluctuation and power angle overshoot under large power variation for better dynamic performance. Moreover, it can improve the dynamic performance (less DC-link voltage fluctuation) not in the cost of the steady-state performance (low-frequency-resonance suppressing capability) by not increasing the loop gain around the equilibrium point. The real-time simulation based on NI-PXI and power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) experiment validate its effectiveness and advantages compared to traditional methodology.

title: V2G Coordination for Secure and Low-Carbon Operation of EV-Rich Distribution Systems: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The increasing popularization of electric vehicles (EVs) offers opportunities to reduce carbon emissions via vehicle-to-grid (V2G) coordination. This paper proposes a secure and low-carbon V2G coordination framework for EV fleets based on the proposed grid-interactive multi-region model (GMM), which characterizes realistic EV operation patterns (e.g., charging, discharging, and driving) impacted by complex V2G coordination and enables accurate impact analysis of EV aggregation on the EV-rich distribution system (ERDS). To effectively learn a secure V2G coordination policy in ERDS with infrequent voltage violation signals, a bounded PID (BPID) Lagrangian safe reinforcement learning (BPID-SRL) method is proposed, aiming to optimize carbon emissions without inducing voltage violations. A Transformer-GNN (TG) agent is then designed to jointly handle the spatiotemporal complexity of V2G coordination in ERDS, thereby enhancing the performance of the proposed BPID-SRL. A case study based on a modified IEEE 33-bus system empirically demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed BPID-SRL and its big potential to exploit V2G coordination for secure and low-carbon operations of ERDS.

title: Fairness and Voltage-Quality Enhancement Through Active–Reactive Dynamic Operating Envelopes in Unbalanced Low-Voltage Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel fairness-aware dynamic operating envelope (DOE) framework for equitable active and reactive power allocations in unbalanced low-voltage (LV) networks with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed method extends proportional fairness from conventional active power definitions to apparent power, allowing customers constrained in active export to contribute via reactive power support. A multi-phase current–voltage optimal power flow (OPF) formulation is developed, incorporating inverter capability constraints, transformer loading limits, and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) mitigation. The VUF is explicitly regularised to address phase-level voltage quality issues arising from asymmetric DER installations and single-phase connections. Time-series simulations on a real-world Australian LV feeder demonstrate that the proposed Fair $(P,Q)$ DOE with explicit VUF regularisation consistently maintains transformer and voltage constraints, reduces VUF below industry guidelines, and improves both fairness and network utilisation compared to existing methods. Results confirm that integrating reactive power flexibility and unbalance-aware fairness metrics enables a more inclusive and power-quality-compliant operation of DER-rich LV networks.

title: Distribution-Level Local Imbalance Market for Multi-Timescale Settlement and Network-Constrained Balancing
abstract: Existing local energy markets (LEMs) and local flexibility markets (LFMs) in distribution systems are primarily designed to facilitate energy trading and alleviate congestion. However, they lack explicit mechanisms for modeling nodal power deviations, pricing marginal imbalance costs, and allocating fast frequency response. This paper proposes a local imbalance market (LIM) that introduces a node-level imbalance formulation and distribution locational imbalance prices (DLIPs), internalizing network constraints and the balancing costs induced by power imbalances. The LIM incorporates a multi-timescale clearing structure where the distribution system operator (DSO) computes minute-level balancing decisions and DLIPs. A frequency response sensitivity matrix (FRSM) allocates second-scale fast-response costs to the nodes that caused the deviations. A native ADMM-based LIM clearing algorithm is designed to achieve scalable, privacy-preserving coordination among prosumers, aggregators, and the DSO without revealing private information. The second-scale allocation algorithm ensures cost causality and budget consistency through real-time measurement and ex-post reconciliation. Case studies on three modified distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed LIM enhances balancing efficiency, preserves participant privacy, and achieves accurate cost attribution under renewable uncertainty. The LIM provides a practical and economically consistent pathway for integrating renewable-rich resources into distribution-level market operations.

title: Federated Heterogeneous-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Flexible Dispatch of Energy Hubs
abstract: Energy hubs (EHs) are important district multi-energy systems that integrate various carriers for energy conversion and storage. For the flexible dispatch of EHs, reinforcement learning (RL) has been a promising solution, capable of effectively and efficiently handling inherent uncertainties within EHs. However, the sample inefficiency issue of RL could lead to computational burden and suboptimal policies. More recently, federated reinforcement learning (FRL) has emerged as a new paradigm that improves sample efficiency by coordinating the learning processes of multiple agents. In this work, we introduce FRL for flexible dispatch of EHs and, specifically, propose a federated heterogeneous-agent reinforcement learning (FHRL) framework to overcome the challenges posed by inter-agent heterogeneity, which could lead to training instability and performance degradation in FRL. Our framework features an adaptive model aggregation method that extracts generalized knowledge of dispatch policies to generate the global model. Furthermore, it incorporates a knowledge transfer mechanism that leverages the generalized knowledge to guide the optimization of each local policy. Extensive experiments confirm our framework outperforms traditional RL and FRL in dispatch costs while demonstrating scalability in a large-scale scenario involving 50 heterogeneous EHs.

title: Power Oscillation Mitigation of Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources in Microgrids Under Unbalanced Faults
abstract: Three-phase four-wire Inverter-Interfaced Distributed Energy Resources (3P4W-DERs) offer significant advantages, including reduced emissions, localized energy production, and enhanced reliability for modern power systems. However, during unbalanced fault conditions, 3P4W-DERs may generate oscillatory active and reactive power components. These oscillations lead to DC-link fluctuations, overcurrent stress on power electronic devices, and potential system instabilities. To mitigate these issues, this paper proposes a Triple Current Controller (TCC) based on positive-, negative-, and zero-sequence components. The TCC is designed to eliminate instantaneous power oscillations while ensuring the generated current remains within safe operating limits, even under severe unbalanced fault conditions. The proposed method eliminates the need for complex sequence extraction techniques, thereby reducing control complexity. Also, a current limiting strategy is integrated into the controller to enforce peak current constraints during fault events. The proposed TCC is adaptive to both grid-connected and islanded modes of microgrid operation. Simulation results confirm the TCC’s ability to suppress active and reactive power oscillations without exceeding current limits under a wide range of unbalanced fault scenarios.

title: Correlation-Exploiting False Data Injection Attack and Corresponding DRL-Based Detection Countermeasure in Partially Observable Grids
abstract: In partially observable power grids, limited knowledge of grid topology and correlated nodal injections presents significant challenges to cybersecurity, complicating the development of stealthy false data injection attacks (FDIAs). To address these issues, this paper proposes an optimization-based and correlation-aware FDIA that remains stealthy under AC state estimation and bypasses bad data detection (BDD) by explicitly incorporating spatio-temporal dependencies among nodal injections. The attack strategy employs a reduced-dimensional measurement matrix and an error covariance matrix to model injection correlations, thereby minimizing operational constraint violations. Correspondingly, a coupled Cubature Kalman Filter approach is characterized to enhance state estimation accuracy and reduce conservatism. To counter such evolving attacks, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based detection mechanism is developed. Extensive validation on IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-bus systems demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness with 99.92%−100% accuracy of the proposed method.

title: A Stable Terminal Mercury Hydride and Its Reactivity To Form Mercury–Metal Bonds
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organomercury hydrides are typically encountered as unstable intermediates in organic transformations. These compounds are conventionally thought to be intrinsically unstable and have eluded isolation in the condensed phase. Here, we report the synthesis, isolation, characterization, and reactivity of an unexpectedly stable arylmercury hydride using a sterically encumbering fluorenyl-hydrindacene scaffold. The arylmercury hydride readily reacts with metalloradicals and metal hydrides to form bimetallic complexes containing unsupported mercury–metal bonds. These results suggest that the instability of mercury hydride compounds is not due to an intrinsic weakness of the mercury–hydrogen bond, but rather their propensity to undergo bimetallic reactions that result in mercury–mercury bond formation.

title: Leveraging Heterogeneous Railway Systems as Virtual Inertia Sources for Grid Frequency Regulation
abstract: The expanding penetration of inverter-based renewable energy generation has significantly reduced grid inertia, intensifying frequency stability challenges in modern power systems. Correspondingly, large-scale electrified railway systems, which are conventionally viewed as passive loads, possess a substantial, yet largely unexploited, resource of kinetic energy with inherent potential to support grid frequency. To harness this potential, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage control framework that reconceptualizes railway fleets as active, deterministic, and dispatchable sources of virtual inertia, turning the kinetic energy inherent in train operation into a resource for grid stability. This framework integrates day-ahead stochastic scheduling of train trajectories with real-time hierarchical control, featuring a centralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) layer at the train dispatch center for global coordination and decentralized local controllers on individual trains for rapid inertial response. A cornerstone of this work is the explicit quantification of the virtual inertia available from each train as a function of its physical momentum. This quantification supports a fine-grained control strategy for heterogeneous fleets, accommodating both high-inertia, flexible freight trains and agile passenger trains with tight scheduling constraints. This adaptive approach maximizes grid support while preserving transportation service quality. Case study results validate the efficacy of the proposed strategy, demonstrating a 57.6% reduction in maximum frequency deviation under high-volatility conditions and an improvement of the frequency nadir by over 1.1 Hz during severe generation loss events, thereby preventing emergency load-shedding. Ultimately, this work establishes a scalable pathway for the synergistic operation of transport and power systems, unlocking an advanced class of controllable loads for resilient grid stabilization.

title: Exact Analytical Solution for Self-Scheduling of Energy Storage With Piecewise Objective and Energy Loss Functions
abstract: The optimal self-scheduling (OSS) problem is fundamental to the economic operation of energy storage resources. Accurately modeling their nonlinear characteristics, such as complementarity constraints or state-dependent efficiency, poses significant computational challenges. To attain tractability, most relevant studies rely on linear or convex approximations, leading to suboptimal operation decisions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an efficient analytical solution method to exactly solve a generic formulation of OSS (G-OSS) with piecewise quadratic objective functions and piecewise linear loss functions, which can model a wide spectrum of practical energy storage with high fidelity. G-OSS is recast as a sequence of single-period parametric programs, and a generalized analytical solution algorithm (G-ASA) is devised to compute closed-form, piecewise-defined optimal solutions via a backward-forward framework. Theoretical analysis guarantees the global optimality of G-ASA for solving G-OSS. Numerical results validate that the G-ASA exhibits high efficiency and scalability, substantially outperforming the prevailing solver-based methods while ensuring global optimality.

title: DRL Energy Management for URT Considering Uncertainties of PV and Train Disturbance
abstract: Integrating photovoltaic (PV) energy into urban rail transit faces challenges due to PV variability and fluctuating train loads, often leading to low PV utilization. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based energy management strategy that dynamically coordinates reversible converters to intelligently redistribute surplus PV energy across multiple power supply sections. The approach incorporates stochastic PV generation and train operation uncertainties into the training process within a Markov decision framework, and leverages day-ahead optimization results to design a time-varying reward mechanism that guides real-time control at per second time. Simulation studies on Qingdao Metro Line 2 show that the proposed method achieves a 4.15% reduction in annual energy consumption, corresponding to 1.7 GWh, and outperforms recent optimization-based methods. To further verify real-time feasibility and control effectiveness, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform using a reduced-scale metro line is developed, on which the trained DRL agent is deployed and shown to achieve energy saving in real-time tests. These results highlight the method’s ability to improve energy efficiency and facilitate greater integration of PV energy under dynamic and uncertain conditions in urban rail transit.

title: Charging Station Pricing and Scheduling With Localized Personal Information via Offloading Computation to EVs
abstract: Rapid electric vehicle (EV) adoption has fueled the swift growth of charging station (CS) networks. Nevertheless, these stations encounter challenges in managing unpredictable user behavior while safeguarding EV owners’ privacy. This study introduces a Master-Follower Collaborative Reinforcement Learning (MFCRL) approach to facilitate the cooperative operation of multiple charging stations (CSs). Within the MFCRL framework, cooperative CSs assume the role of master, while EVs operate as followers. The master offloads training tasks involving private internal states to the followers and conducts training using a globally collected dataset, which remains resilient to unpredictable CS occupancy and aggregates local model updates from the followers. Consequently, RL models trained under this framework demonstrate robust performance by effectively adapting to dynamic electricity prices and variable station occupancy. Experimental results confirm the algorithm’s convergence and effectiveness in maximizing cumulative reward.

title: Enhancing Frequency Regulation for DER Cluster Incorporating Dynamic Topology Reconfiguration: A Parameter-Free Meta-Model Approach
abstract: The frequency regulation capability (FRC) of distributed energy resource (DER) cluster is jointly constrained by DER capacity and power flow (PF) security in distribution networks. To fully exploit the FRC of DER clusters and improve system frequency stability, it is effective to optimize network topology and DER frequency characteristics prior to primary frequency regulation (PFR). However, topology reconfiguration invalidates original PF models, while high penetration of DERs introduces strong nonlinearity and time-varying uncertainty, making the problem difficult to solve, particularly in low-voltage cluster without accurate parameters. This paper proposes an analytical optimization method to enhance the FRC of DER clusters, based on a data-driven PF meta-model. A high-dimensional linear PF model with topology adaptability is constructed via deep neural network (DNN)-reconstructed state-space linear lifting, significantly reducing solution complexity, while the remaining bilinear terms are linearized with the penalty method. Furthermore, a hierarchical multi-timescale control framework is introduced to the optimization, where long-term topology reconfiguration enhances network PFR power carrying capacity and short-term adaptive adjustment of DER frequency characteristics to dynamically respond to FRC changes. Case studies verify that the proposed method significantly improves the FRC of the DER cluster without relying on accurate physical parameters.

title: Flexible Coordination Operation of Grid-Interactive Residential Buildings Based on Learning and Optimization-Assisted Search
abstract: The coordinated operation of grid-interactive residential buildings (GRBs) is essential for enhancing the resilience and reliability of power systems. However, existing studies have not simultaneously considered electricity-heat subsystem scheduling and economic compensation, which can limit the service capability of GRBs and weaken their motivation to provide grid services. To this end, this paper investigates a coordinated operation problem of GRBs that incorporates both electricity-heat subsystem scheduling and economic compensation for participating GRBs. Specifically, we formulate a bi-level coordinated optimization problem for GRBs during periods of providing generation capacity services, where the upper-level economic compensation optimization is associated with the distribution system operator, and the lower-level decision-deviation and quota-tracking error minimization is associated with each GRB. To deal with challenges incurred by uncertainty parameters, implicit dynamics models, and multiple stakeholders, we propose an online distributed coordinated operation approach to solve the formulated problem, based on the high-sample-efficiency reinforcement learning algorithm CrossQ combined with optimization-assisted search. The proposed approach can support multi-stakeholder privacy preservation, coordination scalability, and flexible participation of GRBs. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness, flexibility, and robustness of the proposed approach.

title: Conditional Distributionally Robust Optimization for Look-Ahead Power Dispatch With Heterogeneous Uncertainties
abstract: This paper presents a look-ahead environmental-economic power dispatch model incorporating heterogeneous uncertainties. A novel distributionally robust dispersion control is integrated in the model for managing air pollutant emissions. This control approach captures the spatial and temporal distribution of emissions, aiming to minimize their contribution to air pollutant concentrations. Furthermore, the dispersion condition uncertainty is modeled on a finite support to enhance control robustness. As a result, the traditional infinite-support renewable energy uncertainty is combined with the proposed finite-support dispersion condition uncertainty in a distributionally robust optimization framework. A joint ambiguity set is thus formulated for the two heterogeneous and correlative uncertainties, which addresses the heterogeneity through conditional probability theory and captures the correlation by conditional expectation constraints. To solve the distributionally robust dispatch model, it is first converted into a tractable form that incorporates robust cost constraints, utilizing dual theory of infinite dimensional linear programming. A conditional column and constraint generation method is then developed to tackle the reformulated problem. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dispersion control in improving air quality, and the computational efficiency of our solution methods.

title: Frequency-Domain Characterization of Load Demand From Electrified Highways
abstract: Electrified roadways (ER) equipped with dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) capabilities can patently extend the driving range and reduce the battery size of electric vehicles (EVs). However, due to the spatial arrangement of the transmitter coils in the ER, the DWPT load exhibits frequency content that could excite power system frequency dynamics. In this context, this work aims to study the spectrum of DWPT loads under different traffic conditions. Under simplifying assumptions, we develop statistical models to identify the location and relative magnitude of DWPT load harmonics. Our analysis reveals that the fundamental frequency depends on ER coil spacing and average EV speed. In the worst-case yet unlikely scenario that EVs move in a synchronized fashion, the amplitude of harmonics scales with the EV count. On the contrary, when EVs move freely, harmonics scale with the square root of the EV count. Platoon formations can accentuate harmonics. The spectral content around harmonics decreases in magnitude and increases in bandwidth with the harmonic index. The load of a single EV moving at a time-varying speed can be modeled as a frequency-modulated (FM) signal. Despite the simplifying assumptions, the derived models offer valuable insights for ER planners and grid operators. Dynamic simulations of a modified WECC model with DWPT loads synthesized from realistic EV trajectories and ER specifications corroborate some of these insights.

title: Projected Gradient System-Based Trust-Tech Method for Computing Multiple ACOPF Solutions: Theory and Deterministic Solution Methodology
abstract: A theory-based <underline>P</underline>rojected <underline>G</underline>radient <underline>S</underline>ystem (PGS)-based <underline>Tr</underline>ansformation <underline>U</underline>nder <underline>St</underline>ability-re<underline>T</underline>aining <underline>E</underline>quilibria <underline>Ch</underline>aracterization (Trust-Tech, TT) method, termed PGS-TT, is proposed to systematically and deterministically compute multiple AC Optimal Power Flow (ACOPF) solutions within a feasible component. The theoretical basis for the PGS-TT method is rigorously established, including: (i) a one-to-one correspondence between stable equilibrium points (SEPs) of the PGS and local optimal solutions of ACOPF models; (ii) each feasible component is an invariant set of the PGS and consists of the closures of the stability regions of the SEPs located in that feasible component; (iii) each stability region contains exactly one OPF solution, which eliminates redundant searches for additional OPF solutions within the same stability region; and (iv) the existence conditions of multiple OPF solutions that are linked to the existence of PGS stability boundaries. Theorems and the proposed PGS-TT method are illustrated on 3-bus and 9-bus systems exhibiting multiple local OPF solutions. Additionally, the scalability of the implemented PGS-TT method is discussed based on large-scale systems, with network sizes ranging from 1,888 to 30,000 buses, underscoring its potential for complex power-grid optimization.

title: Accelerating Power Flow Calculation in Hybrid AC/DC Distribution Networks via Decomposition of Partial Control Parameters and State Variables
abstract: To facilitate efficient and robust power flow (PF) analysis in multi-voltage-level hybrid AC/DC distribution networks (HAD-DNs), this letter proposes an accelerated computational method through decomposition of partial control parameters of dual active bridge (DAB) converters and system state variables. First, a comprehensive PF model incorporating voltage source converters (VSCs) and DAB converters is established, explicitly considering their distinct control modes. Then, an optimization approach for DAB control variables based on the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions is introduced, along with a unified iterative method to simultaneously determine system state variables and VSC control parameters. Case studies on HAD-DNs of different scales demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and its improved convergence performance compared with conventional methods.

title: Proactive Resilient UC Against Typhoon-Induced Cascading Failures via a Data-Driven Surrogate
abstract: Extreme weather-driven cascading failures (CFs) in power systems can lead to catastrophic socioeconomic losses, yet integrating CF analysis directly into day-ahead proactive unit commitment (UC) is mathematically intractable. This difficulty arises from representing decision-dependent topology evolution within a tractable UC formulation. To address this challenge, a resilient UC framework is proposed, featuring a data-driven surrogate that encodes CF risks into a tractable polyhedral region. First, overload-induced CF simulations are performed offline across diverse commitment and dispatch states under contingencies. To capture nonlinear CF boundaries in the system's discrete-continuous operating space, a sequential training strategy is employed to construct a surrogate consisting of a series of linear classifiers. This surrogate identifies a polyhedral region with low CF risk, which can be directly integrated into the UC model as linear constraints for CF-aware decision-making. Case studies show that the proposed strategy significantly reduces the expected loss of load by proactively mitigating CF risks with only a marginal increase in operating costs, offering a streamlined yet effective pathway for enhancing power system resilience.

title: Cut-Selection Enhanced Risk-Averse Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming for Economic Dispatch With Carbon Capture Systems
abstract: This paper investigates a multi-stage stochastic economic dispatch problem for power systems with carbon capture systems (MCCSED). The focus is on effectively managing operational risks through a risk-averse approach. To efficiently solve this challenging problem, a cut-selection-enhanced risk-averse stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) algorithm is developed, incorporating an enhanced test of usefulness (ETOU) strategy to remedy the premature discarding of valid cuts inherent in the conventional level 1 (L1) method. Case studies on IEEE 39-bus, 118-bus, and 300-bus systems yield these findings. First, higher carbon capture installation rates enhance risk management through increased storage flexibility. Second, the risk-averse approach reduces tail-risk costs and enables more intuitive parameter tuning than distributionally robust optimization, revealing a consistent two-phase pattern across risk management approaches and underscoring the importance of coordinating risk management and flexibility. Third, the proposed ETOU-L1 method offers competitive convergence by recovering valid cuts usually discarded by the conventional L1 method, while demonstrating scalability for large-scale problems.

title: Secure State Estimation Design for Power Converter Dominated AC Microgrids
abstract: With the rapid expansion of smart devices and the digitalization of microgrids, cyber-attacks have become an increasing concern, posing significant threats to the security and stability of microgrids. Traditional observer-based state estimation methods provide a robust approach to mitigating the impact of cyber-attacks. However, they often suffer from estimation errors when dealing with both unknown disturbances, such as voltage couplings and load conditions, and faulty measurements caused by adversarial sensor attacks. To overcome this challenge, this paper contributes a new secure state estimation method by proposing a novel design of unknown input observers (UIOs) to ensure accurate estimation of microgrid voltages and currents under these adverse conditions. First, the estimation inaccuracy problem is analyzed, followed by a detailed design of the proposed estimation methods. A feasibility study is conducted to validate the practicality of the proposed approach. Furthermore, the stability of the UIO-integrated microgrid control system is evaluated. The effectiveness of the proposed estimation approach is verified through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing on a dSPACE-based platform under various attack scenarios.

title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Protein phosphorylation cascades are essential for cell proliferation. Here, we identify protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) as a key stabilizer of phosphoproteins that is indispensable for hepatocyte proliferation during liver regeneration. PRMT1 is upregulated by epidermal growth factor (EGF) via receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and catalyzes the asymmetric dimethylation (ADMA) modification of SKP1 at the R81 residue. This methylation event disrupts FBXW7 recruitment to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby preventing FBXW7-mediated ubiquitination. Since FBXW7 targets multiple pro-proliferative phosphoproteins, this mechanism prevents their degradation, ensuring the transduction of proliferative signals via phosphorylation cascades. Furthermore, in vivo administration of S-adenosylmethionine, the methyl donor for PRMT-catalyzed methylation, significantly accelerates liver regeneration in both mice and patients. Collectively, these findings establish PRMT1 as a central post-translational regulator of hepatocyte proliferation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for liver diseases.

title: Decision-Focused Continual Learning for Seaport Power--Logistics Scheduling: Generalization Across Varying Tasks
abstract: Power–logistics scheduling in modern seaports typically follows a predict-then-optimize pipeline. To enhance the decision quality of predictions, decision-focused learning has been proposed, which aligns the training of forecasting models with downstream decision outcomes. However, this end-to-end design inherently restricts the value of forecasting models to a specific task structure and therefore generalizes poorly to evolving tasks induced by varying vessel arrivals. We address this gap with a decision-focused continual learning framework that adapts online to a stream of scheduling tasks. Specifically, we introduce Fisher-information-based regularization to enhance cross-task generalization by preserving parameters critical to prior tasks. A differentiable convex surrogate is also developed to stabilize gradient backpropagation. The proposed approach enables learning a decision-aligned forecasting model across a varying task stream with sustainable long-term computational and memory requirements. Experiments calibrated to Jurong Port show improved decision performance and cross-task generalization over existing methods, together with reduced computational cost and a bounded memory footprint.

title: A Two-Layer Identification Method for the Transformer-Feeder-Phase Topology of Low-Voltage Distribution Networks Considering Data Incompleteness
abstract: Accurate topology identification for low-voltage distribution networks (LVDN) is fundamental to achieving precise state estimation and effective system control, but existing methods face challenges such as sensitivity to missing data and high dependence to detection equipment. To address these issues, a two-layer identification method for the transformer-feeder-phase topology of LVDN considering voltage data incompleteness is proposed. First, the clustering method combining Newton-Raphson-based optimizer and Gaussian mixture model (NRBO-GMM) is proposed, which integrates Newton-Raphson gradient optimization and intelligent search mechanism to realize high-precision clustering of user voltage data; second, the multiple time scale adaptive weight allocation strategy for single-day topology identification result is constructed, and the clustering results of different scales are dynamically fused by XGBoost to reduce the instability caused by the missing data and single-day identification error; next, based on the phase identification results from the upper layer, the hierarchical user-feeder identification method based on Jenks natural breaks (JNB) and mean absolute error (MAE) minimization is proposed to gradually analyze the feeder attribution of users. Case studies using voltage data from China is performed, and simulation results show that the method can achieve 100% phase identification accuracy with voltage data that only requires a maximum scale of 6 days and an average data missing rate of 42.93%, and that the accuracy of hierarchical user-feeder relationship identification using 10 days of data with a 41.79% missing rate is more than 95%, and reaches 100% for 26 days and remains at this level thereafter. Additionally, the effectiveness and portability of the proposed method between different distribution networks is validated. Thus, the proposed method provides a high-precision and low data requirement topology identification basis for the digital operation and maintenance of LVDN.

title: Privacy-Preserving Generation Fraud Detection for Distributed Photovoltaic Systems: A Solar Irradiance-Fused Federated Learning Framework
abstract: The wide adoption of residential photovoltaic (PV) systems introduces new challenges for generation fraud detection (FD). Unlike traditional electricity theft detection, which focuses on electricity consumption-side behavior, PV generation fraud detection (PVG-FD) is complicated by the inherent intermittency and uncertainty of PV generation. The distributed nature of PV systems poses further challenges for centralized PVG-FD approaches due to scalability and privacy concerns. This paper develops a privacy-preserving distributed PVG-FD framework based on federated learning (FL). In this framework, a utility company manages multiple household communities, where each of which is equipped with a local detector. The framework integrates a novel detection model architecture with privacy-preserving global collaboration. Each community’s local model fuses PV generation and weather data via a co-attention mechanism to detect discrepancies critical for PVG-FD. The FL framework enables cross-community collaboration by aggregating model parameters and prototypes, leveraging global knowledge sharing with local refinement while preserving privacy. It also uses prototype alignment to address class imbalance by enhancing fraud sample representation. Extensive experiments on a real-world residential PV dataset validate the effectiveness of the developed method and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art FL methods across various scenarios. The results also show its scalability across varying community sizes and strong robustness to class imbalance.

title: Edge AI-Enabled PMU Event Classification With Knowledge Distillation and Federated Learning
abstract: Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) enable analysis and classification of events and abnormalities in modern power systems. However, in large and geographically dispersed networks, centralizing PMU data streams for sub-second decisions is hindered by cross-regional data-sharing restrictions, multi-layer aggregation, as well as communication delays and jitter. Purely local training at the network edge on the PMU devices themselves can avoid these bottlenecks but lacks exposure to diverse operating conditions, leading to suboptimal models. This tension calls for methods that retain data locality and privacy while sharing knowledge efficiently. To this end, this paper proposes an edge AI framework that integrates knowledge distillation and federated learning, driven by the core requirement of different data-sharing constraints. First, we assume a trusted data center, where we develop a large language model-based teacher model that is fine-tuned on global data and efficiently transfers knowledge into student models trained locally via knowledge distillation. Next, we relax such an assumption and design a fair federated learning framework that exchanges gradient information among edge models while enforcing Pareto-optimal fairness to ensure stable and balanced performance. We also customize a lightweight neural network tailored for on-device deployment. With fewer than 5,000 parameters, the model adopts a compact end-to-end architecture to effectively characterize temporal dynamics and frequency-domain information in PMU time series, thereby achieving both high efficiency and strong representational capability. Experiments conducted on real-world PMU measurements demonstrate the superior performance of our framework, and ablation studies further confirm the unique contributions of each design component.

title: Sensing-Communication-Computing Integrated Resource Allocation for 3D Observability Enhancement of Distribution Grid
abstract: To address poor observability of distribution grid under constrained communications, this paper proposes a three-dimensional (3D) observability enhancement framework under sensing-communication-computing integration. It builds a 3D observability model covering numerical, temporal, and spatial dimensions, which are quantified via dynamic time warping (DTW) sequence similarity, sensed data peak age of information (PAoI), and unobservable extreme event ratios. For sensing, scenarized cascading inter-dependencies between electrical equipment states are leveraged, significantly improving distributed learning convergence while enabling event-driven accurate data sensing. For transmission, the proposed algorithm infers device-server-channel matching preferences via bounded Q-matching, and addresses the externality dilemma caused by co-channel interference coupling with signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) bound violation-driven swap operations. For computing, an age of information (AoI)-greedy heuristic mechanism iteratively allocates resources by prioritizing data computing needs of devices with higher AoI proportions. Simulations verify its effectiveness in improving 3D observability, distributed photovoltaic absorption, and economic energy dispatch.

title: Assessment of Sequential Frequency Regulation Potential of Polysilicon Loads Under Weak Observability via Inverse-Optimization
abstract: High renewable penetration has increased the demand for flexible frequency regulation resources in power systems. As an energy-intensive upstream sector of the photovoltaic manufacturing chain, the polysilicon industry has considerable frequency regulation potential. However, its reliable assessment is challenged by weak observability of production states and the lack of a clear sequential response mechanism. This paper proposes a method to assess the sequential frequency regulation potential of polysilicon loads under weak observability based on inverse optimization. First, a state-task-network-based process model is developed to describe the coupling between production states and electricity consumption. Then, an inverse-optimization-based state estimation model is constructed, in which typical disturbance scenarios are incorporated to enhance robustness. Finally, the continuous regulation potential and economic performance over multiple time intervals are evaluated by considering temporal coupling and response aversion costs. Case studies show that the proposed method yields regulation capacity estimates close to the theoretical upper bound under full-information conditions while satisfying production constraints, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness and economic viability.

title: Robust Observer-Enhanced Resilient Control of Grid-Following LCL Inverters Under Cyber Sensor Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a robust proportional–integral (PI) control strategy with an observer for grid-following (GFL) inverters modeled as cyber–physical systems (CPS), designed to withstand denial-of-service (DoS) and intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) attacks targeting sensors and controllers. Such attacks can corrupt sensor measurements, cause communication delays and outages, degrade control performance, and even destabilize the system. In contrast to existing control approaches, the proposed method explicitly mitigates the detrimental effects of both DoS and IEMI attacks. The observer and PI controller gains are co-designed using linear matrix inequality (LMI) based optimization, ensuring robust stability under attack scenarios. Control and estimation processes are implemented within a time-triggered framework to guarantee deterministic timing and enable rigorous stability analysis. Furthermore, a residual-based fault and attack detection scheme employing fixed thresholds and hysteresis is introduced to promptly identify and isolate compromised sensors or communication links. Once an attack is detected, the system switches to healthy measurements or substitutes observer estimates to preserve stable operation. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through real-time hardware experiments and MATLAB/Simulink simulations using a laboratory-scale grid-connected inverter. The results demonstrate the method’s strong resilience and stability against IEMI and DoS attacks compared with conventional control strategies.

title: A Behavioral-Strategic Market Mechanism for Energy Sharing: Integrating LLM-Driven Bounded Rationality With Regulatory Optimization
abstract: Energy sharing markets facilitate collaborative energy exchange among prosumers, yet their theoretical efficiency is often compromised by bounded rationality. Existing regulatory mechanisms, predicated on the assumption of perfect rationality, mathematically mask this non-linear cognitive friction, leaving grid operators vulnerable to unstructured behavioral instabilities. To bridge this gap, we propose a Bi-Level Regulatory Optimization Framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) as a “surrogate behavioral stress-testing” environment.
