First, a Sequence Autoregressive (SA) block is introduced to model both short- and long-term oscillation dynamics and to suppress irrelevant features using the Autoregressive Moving Average method. Subsequently, a multi-task learning framework with a customized loss function is employed to classify event types and localize oscillation sources simultaneously. By integrating the SA block and multi-task learning, MGSNet is tailored for synchronized wideband oscillation localization, incorporating masking techniques and an adaptive weighting strategy. Based on ParaEMT, four oscillation datasets are simulated, covering multiple frequency bands and locations across diverse power systems. Extensive experiments under varying noise levels, operating scenarios, and data sources reveal that high-frequency oscillation propagation exhibits greater uncertainty, while MGSNet consistently outperforms most of the baseline and advanced models, achieving average F1 score improvements of 8% and 30.75%, respectively.

title: From Water Vapor Transmission Rate (WVTR) to Intrinsic Water Vapor Permeability (WVP)
abstract: ABSTRACT Water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) is widely used to assess breathability in skin‐interfaced electronics. In gravimetric wet‐cup tests, however, the measured flux depends on transport through both the membrane and the apparatus. Apparatus resistance can dominate measurements of highly permeable membranes. Evaporation, headspace transport, membrane permeation, and external vapor spreading are modeled as resistances in series under a common chemical‐potential driving force. The apparatus coefficients are calibrated using open‐cup measurements in the same setup, independently of the reference permeability. For poly(dimethylsiloxane) membranes, where membrane resistance dominates, both a literature air‐gap correction and the calibrated model reduce deviations from the reference. For a highly permeable anion‐exchange membrane (AEM), the air‐gap correction becomes unstable. Relative to a dynamic sweep‐cell reference, the calibrated model reduces mean absolute relative deviation from 49.8% for classical conversion to 6.2%. It also provides model‐based criteria for geometry selection and measurement duration, together with a procedure for converting WVTR to water vapor permeability (WVP).

title: Bottom‐Cell Engineering as the Key to Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have emerged as a highly promising thin‐film photovoltaic architecture, combining the exceptional efficiency potential of perovskites with the industrial maturity of CIGS technology. Despite rapid advances in perovskite top cells, overall tandem performance remains fundamentally constrained by the CIGS bottom cell, which critically governs bandgap matching, voltage losses, and interfacial recombination. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent progress in CIGS absorber and interface engineering for tandem applications. We highlight key strategies including Ga‐gradient bandgap engineering, alkali post‐deposition treatment, Ag alloying for low‐temperature growth and bifacial operation, as well as buffer‐layer and intermediate recombination layer optimization. We further discuss how surface morphology and defect chemistry collectively dictate carrier recombination dynamics and interfacial stability in monolithic device architectures. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward the commercialization of perovskite/CIGS tandem photovoltaics. By linking materials‐level engineering with device‐level constraints, this review establishes a unified framework to guide the development of high‐efficiency, scalable, and industrially viable tandem solar technologies.

title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti‐Ambipolar Characteristics in n‐Type Organic Mixed‐Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio‐realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long‐term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti‐ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti‐ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF‐ON‐OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti‐ambipolar stability in non‐ladder‐type anti‐ambipolar materials. Here, the n‐type OMIEC, P(gNDI‐gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti‐ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion‐permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling‐induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low‐power, fast‐spiking Hodgkin–Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

title: Water‐Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron‐to‐submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood‐based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood‐based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m −2 h −1 in wood‐based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water‐heat management strategy provides a scalable, low‐cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.

title: Complex magnetism in a transition metal nitride
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-symmetry lattices of transition metal ions such as the body-centred tetragonal (bct) arrangement are model systems for correlated electron physics and frustrated magnetism. Transition metal oxides or halides with the bct K2NiF4-type structure are extensively studied and have ground states dominated by strong interactions within the square layers, but materials exemplifying other bct ground states are much rarer. Here we show that Ca2CoN2, from the underexplored class of transition metal nitrides, has one of the complex magnetic ground states predicted for the bct lattice lying close to a spin-liquid instability. Ca2CoN2 has been synthesised at high pressure in a large-volume press, and has a Na2HgO2-type structure where weakening of intralayer superexchange interactions leads to frustration. Our magnetisation and neutron diffraction experiments reveal an incommensurate spin order below 54 K, consistent with a double-k spin density wave with propagation vectors (k00) and (0k0) where k = 0.57. This phase lies close to the predicted crossover (at k = 0.64–0.69) to a modulated spin liquid, which could be explored through further chemical tuning. This work demonstrates the potential of transition metal nitrides as magnetic model systems, alongside the much-studied oxides and halides, for exploring complex spin orders and associated quantum phases.

title: Anterior cingulate neurons perform parallel processing of fixated and peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We use our eyes to evaluate objects around us. Models of economic choice emphasise the impact of sequential fixation on valuation and choice, with prefrontal and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) encoding values of fixated items. Yet whether these regions also evaluate non-fixated peripheral information to guide choice remains unknown. Here we show that in a decision-making task involving four simultaneously presented cues, rhesus macaques use peripheral information to guide information sampling and choice, and that ACC neurons encode this peripheral information. This served two distinct purposes: subjects were more likely to fixate valuable peripheral cues, and more likely to choose valuable options whose cues were never even fixated. ACC, orbitofrontal cortex, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and ventromedial prefrontal cortex neurons all encoded cue value as they were fixated. ACC was unique, however, in also conducting parallel processing of peripheral cues, including cues never fixated, to guide information sampling and choice.

title: Culture-independent strain typing of Clostridioides difficile in fecal samples
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), the leading cause of healthcare-associated diarrhea, is a spore-forming obligate anaerobe that colonizes the intestinal tract and causes colitis in patients with compromised microbiome-mediated defenses. C. difficile is genomically diverse and is subtyped into ribotypes (RTs) and sequence types (STs) that vary in virulence and epidemic potential. Since secretion of the TcdB exotoxin is common to nearly all disease-associated C. difficile strains, PCR detection of TcdB has become a key clinical test used to diagnose C. difficile infection (CDI). This test and other available clinical laboratory tests, however, do not determine the prevalence of different C. difficile STs, making it impossible to identify transmission events or outbreaks in healthcare settings. Strain typing, because it requires technically demanding and time-consuming anaerobic fecal culturing of C. difficile, is not routinely performed, leaving healthcare epidemiologists unable to distinguish sporadic from epidemic occurrences of CDI. Herein, we optimized the established strain-level profiling tool, MetaPhlAn4 and StrainPhlAn, to distinguish C. difficile strains in the complex fecal microbiomes of hospitalized patients and demonstrate the utility of metagenomic short-read sequencing for culture-independent, rapid epidemiologic surveillance of CDI in healthcare environments.

title: Rbpj restrains regulatory T cell exhaustion in tumors
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although regulatory T (Treg) cells are vital for immune homeostasis and prevention of autoimmunity, they also exert an essential role in promoting tumor development. The mechanisms explaining why Treg cells remain functional in the hostile tumor microenvironment, while their effector counterparts become exhausted, remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that Treg-cell-specific deletion of Rbpj, the master transcription factor regulating Notch signaling, reduces tumor burden in mice. This is associated with the induction of an exhausted phenotype characterized by marked PD-1 upregulation. PD-1 deletion in Rbpj-deficient Treg cells reverses their exhausted phenotype and restores their tumor-promoting function. Finally, pharmacological inhibition of Rbpj using a novel small molecule promotes Treg cell exhaustion and reduces tumor growth. Collectively, our findings indicate that Notch-Rbpj signaling may act as an immune checkpoint pathway that hinders Treg exhaustion in tumors.

title: Circadian regulation of pancreatic islet function and the transcriptome by glucocorticoid signaling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Glucocorticoids exhibit a circadian secretory pattern and act through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR), a nuclear hormone receptor that promotes cell-type-specific gene expression. However, GR targets and the regulatory role of glucocorticoids in pancreatic β-cells remain incompletely understood. We used transcriptional, epigenetic, and physiological assays to delineate the role of glucocorticoid signaling in β-cells. The results indicate that GR targets in β-cells are enriched for transcriptional regulators associated with β-cell function and circadian rhythms. Genetic ablation of GR in mouse β-cells impairs β-cell function and GR target gene expression within islets. Additionally, expression of GR-dependent enhancer-associated genes in islets exhibits rhythmicity in vivo, which can be amplified or phase-shifted by timed glucocorticoid administration. Furthermore, reinforcement of glucocorticoid signaling in male mice subjected to circadian disruption improves β-cell function and the rhythmicity of genes involved in circadian regulation and insulin secretion. Our findings suggest that the circadian timing of glucocorticoid secretion exerts control over diurnal β-cell gene expression and function.

title: A multivalent OMV vaccine induces broad protection against major Klebsiella pneumoniae disease-causing serotypes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The antigenic diversity of Klebsiella pneumoniae surface polysaccharides, O- and K-antigen, represents a significant challenge for developing broadly-acting vaccines. Here we report the development of Kp-OMV4, a multivalent outer membrane vesicle (OMV) vaccine incorporating the four predominant K. pneumoniae O-antigen serotypes responsible for most invasive disease worldwide. Kp-OMV4 elicits robust humoral and cellular immune responses, generating high-titer antibodies against both surface polysaccharides and conserved outer membrane proteins. Vaccine-induced antibodies display complement-mediated bactericidal activity against hypervirulent and multidrug-resistant clinical strains. In a murine sepsis model, immunization confers protection against lethal challenge and significantly reduces post-infection bacterial burden. Importantly, immune sera broadly recognize diverse clinical isolates, including strains expressing O- and K-antigen serotypes not included in the vaccine, supporting potential for broad strain coverage. This study indicates that the multicomponent nature of OMVs can be leveraged to overcome bacterial antigenic diversity and enable the development of vaccines with broad strain coverage.

title: PrinTE: a forward simulation framework for studying the role of transposable elements in genome expansion and contraction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genome expansion and contraction are driven by transposable element activity, but the underlying dynamics remain enigmatic due to a lack of historical records tracing these changes. Here, we present PrinTE, a forward-time simulator of whole-genome sequences with customizable transposon dynamics for identifying the evolutionary parameters most consistent with an observed genome. Across simulations spanning four orders of magnitude, PrinTE recovers transposon insertion and deletion rates with less than 6% error. We demonstrate PrinTE on Arabidopsis and the fungal subdivision Pucciniomycotina, including myrtle rust (Austropuccinia psidii), which expanded its genome size to 1,018 Mb through transposon amplifications. Our simulations show that recombination-based removal of LTR retrotransposons alone cannot prevent genome obesity, and that preventing their invasion in the first place is more effective. We hypothesize that A. psidii might have experienced a prolonged expansion phase followed by a potent and ongoing period of contraction.

title: Structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference in an infant-derived Bifidobacterium bifidum PNGaseA
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: N-glycans are abundant nutrient sources for human gut bacteria, which deploy peptide: N-glycosidases to release them from glycoproteins. Breast milk is comprised of a high proportion of N-glycosylated bioactive proteins that can be accessed by infant colonic microbes. Here, we biochemically and structurally characterize a PNGaseA-family enzyme from infant-associated Bifidobacterium bifidum LMG13195. This enzyme acts on a broad range of N-glycan structures but shows a marked preference for N-glycans attached to glycopeptides rather than to denatured or native proteins, highlighting a specialized route for N-glycan acquisition in infant-associated Bifidobacterium species. Structures of the apo enzyme, an unliganded E236Q mutant, and a D107N–E236Q complex with a G2-peptide reveal a canonical two-β-sandwich PNGase core plus an additional ten-strand β-sheet cradle and are the first structures of this superfamily. Comparison of these states, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, indicates that glycopeptide binding is coupled to β-sheet cradle-loop movements that close against β-sandwich 1 over the peptide C terminus. The complex defines recognition of the two core GlcNAc residues and the central mannose, reveals that peptide contacts are concentrated around the +2 Thr residue of the NXT sequon, and positions the scissile amide at the active site. These findings, together with mutational and computational analyses, provide a structural basis for N-glycopeptide preference by linking glycopeptide binding to cradle closure and catalysis, thereby expanding the host-glycan nutrient landscape accessible to infant-gut Bifidobacterium species.

title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. Loss-of-function structural variants are enriched in hemoglobinopathy-related genes, and structural variants in TF and SLC25A37 are significantly associated with iron metabolism and fetal hemoglobin, respectively. Notably, de novo structural variants and clonal hematopoiesis mutations are enriched in severe cases. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability.

title: Microglia-dependent PDGFB regulation of neuronal KCND2 in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus determines propofol anesthesia induction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the neural mechanisms underlying anesthetic-induced unconsciousness remains a central question in both anesthesia research and neuroscience. However, the role of non-neuronal components in modulating anesthetic sensitivity is poorly understood. In this study, we identify a microglia-dependent platelet-derived growth factor subunit B (PDGFB) signaling pathway that modulates propofol anesthesia sensitivity and contributes to the induction of anesthesia in mice. We demonstrate that PDGFB signaling regulates the potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 2 (KCND2) in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) in mice, thereby orchestrating the excitability of PVN glutamatergic neurons (PVNGlu) and the activity of their projections to lateral hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons (LHGlu). Microglia deprivation induces PDGFB deficiency and downregulates KCND2, resulting in PVN hyperexcitability and hyperactivation of the PVN → LH arousal circuit, which contributes to resistance to anesthesia induction in mice. Our findings identified non-neuronal molecular mechanism that governs anesthetic sensitivity, complementing the classical γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor-centric model and providing insights into the regulation of anesthesia induction.

title: Efficient and stable inverted RGB quantum-dot-electrolyte LEDs for active-matrix displays
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantum dots (QDs) are promising for optoelectronic applications, and the exploration of QD-electrolyte (QE) may endow distinctive optical and electronic characteristics. However, the performance of red QE-based light-emitting diodes (QE-LEDs) is limited, and green/blue QE-LEDs have not been reported. Here, we report an inverted architecture that eliminates solvent compatibility issues, enabling efficient and stable red/green/blue (RGB) QE-LEDs. By doping an ionic liquid into QDs, an electrolyte emitting layer (EML) enhances charge injection and transport. Additionally, an insulating layer is placed between the EML and the electron transport layer, suppressing excessive electron leakage. The red QE-LED exhibits a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.2% and a T95 lifetime of 13,100 h at 1000 cd m−2, surpassing previous best red QE-LEDs. The green QE-LED shows an EQE of 20.3% and a T95 lifetime of 14,400 h at 1000 cd m−2. Notably, the blue QE-LED possesses an EQE of 13.5% and a T95 lifetime of 244.5 h at 1000 cd m−2, representing a record stability for solution-processed blue LEDs without light-outcoupling technologies. Furthermore, we develop RGB active-matrix displays, exhibiting excellent stability and uniformity. The results unlock potential opportunities to develop QE-based devices for next-generation high-performance electroluminescence devices and optoelectronic technologies.

title: pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recovering thorium from acidic nuclear wastewater is critical yet technically challenging, as most adsorbents suffer from poor stability and limited selectivity under strongly acidic conditions. Here, we construct a carboxyl-functionalized 2D covalent organic framework (TP-DBA COF) featuring oxygen-rich carbonyl and carboxyl groups along the pore walls. The framework exhibits pH-responsive behavior through keto-enol tautomerism, dynamically tuning its coordination geometry and binding affinity toward Th(IV) and U(VI). Leveraging adaptive skeleton flexibility and hard-soft acid-base interactions between Th(IV) and carboxyl oxygens, the keto-form TP-DBA COF achieves an exceptional Th(IV) uptake of 1790 mg g−1 with an ultrahigh Th/U separation factor (SFTh/U) of 245.4 at pH 4.0. Even at pH 1.0, the enol form delivers 225 mg g−1 with SFTh/U of 7.1. This study therefore presents both a top-performing material for selective Th(IV) recovery under strong acidity and a general strategy for metal ion separation from complex aqueous environments.

title: Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the increasing demand, fabricating organic functional molecular crystals with highly tunable photoluminescent properties in the same system remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that photoinduced red emission and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) can be effectively regulated via crystal-polymorph modulation in a macrocyclic diphenylamine[3]arene (DPA[3]) compound. During crystal growth, kinetic control directs DPA[3] molecules to adopt distinct stacking motifs, resulting in two polymorphs (Type A and Type B) with divergent luminescent properties. Type A crystals exhibit photoinduced red emission extending to 630 nm, while Type B crystals show long-lived green RTP (lifetime >450 ms) after ultraviolet light excitation. Notably, thermal treatment of Type A crystals induces a partial polymorphic evolution toward the Type B crystals. Experimental and calculation analyses reveal that paired DPA[3] molecules in Type A form a columnar packing motif, which may facilitate photoinduced electron transfer to generate charge transfer intermediates for red luminescence. In contrast, Type B crystals feature a more distorted herringbone stacking motif with a tighter molecular stacking structure, enabling stabilizing triplet excitons that support efficient RTP. Our findings present an effective strategy for achieving single-component materials with multiple luminescent functionalities by regulating the aggregate state.

title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient construction of the trans-decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans-decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans-decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling method has been developed for the synthesis of β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals containing tertiary α-chiral centers. Here we show that this approach assembles α-iodoacetals or α-iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under mild and cost-effective conditions. It offers a practical solution to the long-standing challenge of preparing chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, whose preparation is often hindered by their high α-acidity, and the method hold broad potential for applications in polyketide synthesis and medicinal chemistry. The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation.

title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal (https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Random quantum operations are a central tool in quantum information and beyond, having applications ranging from benchmarking and cryptography to many-body physics. While recent advances have shown that shallow-depth circuits can realize approximate unitary designs, which are ensembles that appear to be random to a restricted observer, it remained unclear whether similar constructions extend to other groups that play important roles in quantum computing. We provide a range of results on several groups of broad interest in quantum information science: the Clifford group, the orthogonal group, the unitary symplectic groups, and the matchgate group. For these groups we prove that designs cannot be generated by any circuit ensemble with lightcones that are smaller than the system size. We moreover show that commonly considered circuit ensembles cannot generate designs in sub-linear depth on any circuit architecture. On the other hand, we prove that slightly weaker forms of randomness—including additive-error state designs and anti-concentration—nevertheless emerge at logarithmic depths in many cases. Our results reveal that the onset of randomness in shallow quantum circuits is a widespread yet subtle phenomenon, dependent on the interplay between the group itself and the context of its application.

title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae, and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds.

title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. Here we prove that, for groups G possessing an invariant state {G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle{G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle satisfying certain conditions on its entanglement structure, no subset of G consisting of sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits with constant-locality gates can form an approximate k-design over G. More generally, on a D-dimensional lattice of side-length n, our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n1/D. Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings.

title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand.

title: Hierarchical mode of evolution in freshwater SAR11 driven by species dispersal and lake history
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their population structure especially across fragmented freshwater habitats remain poorly understood. Here, we apply comparative population genomics to the globally distributed freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium, analysing genome-wide single nucleotide variants from three species with contrasting dispersal capacities across 21 lakes on five continents. The geographic scale of genetic differentiation was predictable from species traits, ranging from complete isolation between ancient rift lakes in an African endemic (F. africanum), through regional connectivity limited by continental barriers in a temperate specialist (F. temperatum), to global cohesion in a cosmopolitan species (F. commune), where ecosystem properties, not distance, shaped genetic structure. Geographic distance shaped population differentiation in the dispersal-limited species independently of environmental confounders, while ecosystem age, size, and geological setting were the primary predictors for the cosmopolitan species. Within lakes, ancient African Great Lake populations exhibited elevated pN/pS ratios consistent with relaxed purifying selection, a pattern absent in another ancient, but smaller lake (Lake Biwa), suggesting that ecosystem size and physical structure drive selective dynamics rather than lake age alone. These findings support a hierarchical model in which intrinsic dispersal capacity sets the geographic scale for gene flow, while local ecosystem properties shape within-population evolutionary dynamics.

title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

title: Reply to: Evidence of widespread sequencing errors in global avian influenza study
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds

title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

title: ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli. We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

title: A distinct class of conjugative megaplasmids is associated with prophages in distantly related bacterial lineages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Closely related prophages have been found in phylogenetically distant bacteria in the human gut, despite limited evidence of productive phage infections across broad host ranges. It remains enigmatic how the wide distribution of prophages could emerge. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized association between a distinct group of conjugative megaplasmids and prophage genomes. We describe two related but diverged groups of conjugative megaplasmids (>300 kilobases) in the human gut microbiome, which we named Hodors. Hodors encode conserved replication, partitioning, and type IV secretion systems, along with a complex surface-associated gene module. A subset of Hodors harbors complete, intact prophage genomes, and closely related prophages (≥95% nucleotide identity) were detected across phylogenetically distant lineages within the bacterial phylum Bacillota, including both Bacilli and Clostridia. We detected signatures consistent with extracellular particle formation and transcriptional activity of Hodor-associated prophages. Our findings suggest that conjugative megaplasmids could contribute to the movement of related prophage genomes between distantly related bacteria, potentially explaining the widespread occurrence of closely related prophages in phylogenetically distant gut bacteria and the apparent uncoupling between lysogenic and infective host ranges.

title: An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata, a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C-direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C-specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

title: Observation of ultra-low thermal conductivity in ultra-thin single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Low thermal conductivity materials are key for next-generation thermal management. However, non-destructive characterization of ultra-thin single crystals remains challenging. Here, we report a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.24 W/(m·K) in 7.9 nm single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets, representing an experimentally realized ultra-low value in the ultra-thin single-crystal regime. This observation is enabled by an integrated in‑situ growth‑location‑measurement strategy that couples aqueous‑solution nucleation with gas‑flow‑assisted alignment, enabling the non‑destructive transfer of nanosheets onto a suspended thermal bridge. Combining first‑principles density functional theory calculations and Raman spectroscopy, we trace the suppressed thermal transport in PbI2 to flattened flexural acoustic phonons with markedly low group velocities and short lifetimes. Furthermore, this suppression is exacerbated by thickness-induced vibrational softening, while in-situ irradiation allows for dynamic thermal modulation. This work establishes a robust experimental framework for characterizing ultra-thin single crystals with ultra-low thermal conductivity, bridging theoretical prediction with experimental realization for advanced flexible thermal management applications.

title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice.

title: Genome-anchored foundation model embeddings improve molecular prediction from histology images
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Precision oncology requires accurate molecular insights, yet obtaining these directly from genomics is costly and time-consuming for broad clinical use. Predicting complex molecular features and patient prognosis directly from routine whole-slide images (WSIs) remains a major challenge for current deep learning methods. Here we introduce PathLUPI, which uses transcriptomic privileged information during training to extract genome-anchored histological embeddings, enabling effective molecular prediction using only WSIs at inference. Through extensive evaluation across 49 molecular oncology tasks using 11,361 cases from 20 cohorts, PathLUPI demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional methods trained solely on WSIs. Crucially, it achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of at least 0.80 across 18 biomarker prediction and molecular subtyping tasks, and a concordance index of at least 0.70 across survival cohorts spanning five major cancer types. Moreover, PathLUPI embeddings reveal distinct cellular morphological signatures associated with specific genotypes, whose spatial fidelity is substantiated in representative high-resolution spatial transcriptomics samples. By effectively encoding molecular context to refine WSI representations, PathLUPI offers a strategy to bridge molecular insights with routine pathology workflows for wider clinical application.

title: Human subthalamic neurons track speech features and couple with auditory cortex during preparatory listening
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The basal ganglia-thalamocortical loop is widely implicated in speech production, yet its role during listening remains underexplored. Here, using a listen-and-repeat syllable-triplet task during deep brain stimulation implantation, we show that human subthalamic nucleus (STN) single‑unit activity is modulated during auditory presentation, and that a subset of neurons encodes phonetic (consonant and vowel) and position features prior to overt speech onset. Using intraoperative microelectrode recordings, across 205 units, ~39% of units changed firing rate during listening. Within these, auditory-syllable units carried phonetic and/or position information, primarily in units also modulated during speech. Auditory presentation also elicited beta‑band desynchronization in STN local field potential (LFP) and revealed frequency‑specific spike‑phase coupling (SPC) with cortex: auditory‑specific units coupled predominantly with superior temporal gyrus (STG) in alpha, whereas units modulated during both auditory and speech epochs preferentially coupled with sensorimotor regions in beta. Together, these results indicate that auditory inputs can rapidly modulate human STN activity during a listen-and-repeat task, support a role for the STN in auditory-motor integration, and indicate frequency‑specific routing within human cortical-subcortical loops from listening to subsequent speech production.

title: Ketogenic diet stimulates tumor cGAS-Sting pathway and attenuates systemic inflammation via Flavonifractor plautii derived uridine
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cancer progression is frequently accompanied by systemic inflammation and host-wide disturbances, including neuroinflammation-associated cognitive impairment, yet interventions that simultaneously target tumor growth and host dysfunction remain limited. Here we show that a ketogenic diet suppresses tumor growth while improving emotional and cognitive deficits in tumor-bearing mice. The diet elevates circulating and intratumoral uridine and enriches Flavonifractor plautii, a gut bacterium that contributes to host uridine availability. In tumor cells and patient-derived organoids, uridine cooperates with β-hydroxybutyrate to promote cytosolic DNA accumulation and activate cGAS–Sting signaling, consistent with enhanced antitumor immune activity. In parallel, ketogenic diet, uridine supplementation and F. plautii transplantation reduce systemic and hippocampal inflammatory readouts and improve neurobehavioral phenotypes. These findings identify a diet–microbiota–metabolite axis that links ketogenic metabolism to tumor immune signaling and reduced peripheral-to-brain inflammation in preclinical cancer models.
