abstract: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and water bodies and pairing upper and lower reservoirs under land-use, protection and grid-distance constraints. The reproducible workflow uses open pan-European data, a hybrid terrain stack (FABDEM; national lidar in Norway and Sweden) and an explicit allowable water-level variation for lake volume. At a 5-km grid distance and 1-m drawdown, exact maximum-weight matching gives an all-size screened bound of 2.57 TWh; excluding mapped-karst footprints for purpose-built reservoirs and sites above 2500 m leaves 0.58 TWh, of which a 21 115-site portfolio capped at 100 MWh per site stores 0.40 TWh (0.24 TWh, EU-27). Replacing FABDEM by national lidar cuts Norway’s and Sweden’s screened energy with 72% each (328.7 to 92.1 and 67.3 to 18.5 GWh): usable lake volume barely moves ( − 0.4 %), but pairs containing a dry basin collapse because that basin binds. A Sobol analysis makes maximum pair distance and karst treatment the joint controls (total effects 0.49 and 0.48). This is an exploratory first screening, not deployable capacity: it ranks where national feasibility studies should look, and their constraints can only reduce it.

source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The current understanding of zeolite crystallization is still far from well understood. Herein, we show that the crystallization pathway of high-silica ZSM-5, one of the most industrially important zeolites, can be altered not only by the type of organic structure-directing agents (OSDAs) at a gel Si/Al ratio of 50 but also by the simultaneous use of Na+ and Cs+ ions as inorganic structure-directing agents (ISDAs). The use of the diquaternary OSDA 1,8-bis(N-methylpyrrolidinium)octane (1,8-MPO) instead of tetrapropylammonium (TPA), the most common OSDA for the synthesis of ZSM-5, in the presence of Na+ led to zeolite β as an intermediate phase; otherwise, no crystalline intermediate was observed. Also, the addition of a small amount of Cs+ ions (gel Cs/Na = 0.14) as a secondary ISDA to the 1,8-MPO-Na+ and TPA-Na+ systems gave small-pore zeolites bikitaite and analcime as an intermediate phase during synthesis, respectively. More importantly, we found that the framework Al distribution in the final product ZSM-5 could differ according to the in situ transformation pathway of intermediate phases, as well as to the type of OSDA used. This study provides a new strategy for directly controlling the intrazeolitic location of Brønsted acid sites, as well as the nucleation pathway in the synthesis of high-silica zeolites.

A Dual-Function Electrolyte Additive Suppresses Mn Crosstalk for Durable High-Temperature Graphite/LiMn2O4 Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mn crosstalk accelerates the degradation of graphite/LiMn2O4 (LMO) batteries, particularly at elevated temperatures, through the migration and deposition of dissolved Mn species on the graphite anode, which destabilizes the anode interphase. Here, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) suppresses this cross-electrode degradation pathway by regulating both the bulk electrolyte chemistry and the LMO/electrolyte interface. In the bulk electrolyte, the Si–O groups of TMSP consume HF and suppress continued HF generation through LiPF6 hydrolysis, thereby weakening acid-induced LMO corrosion. At the cathode interface, preferential adsorption and oxidation of TMSP promote the formation of a thin (∼3 nm) Li3PO4-rich cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), which limits electrolyte decomposition and Mn dissolution. These complementary effects reduce Mn dissolution and deposition on the graphite anode, thereby limiting Mn-associated SEI growth and resistance increase. In 1.6 Ah graphite/LMO 18650 cells, 2.1 wt % TMSP reduces Mn deposition on the anode by 95.2% and increases capacity recovery from 90.5% to 95.1% after storage at 60 °C for 7 days. The cells also retain 80.2% of their initial capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C and 45 °C. These results establish the suppression of Mn crosstalk as an effective strategy for improving the high-temperature durability of graphite/LMO batteries.

title: Conductive Composite-Based Wearable Sensors for Sports Science: Intelligent Data Analysis and Emerging Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Wearable sensors enable continuous acquisition of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals during exercise, providing data to support sports performance assessment, training regulation, fatigue monitoring, and rehabilitation interventions. However, signal reliability and multidimensional data analysis under complex motion conditions remain constrained by device functionality. Conductive composites can improve sensor flexibility, interfacial conformability, and signal acquisition performance, while artificial intelligence (AI) enables movement pattern recognition, state assessment, and outcome prediction from complex data. Their integration is advancing wearable systems toward multimodal sensing and intelligent analysis. Guided by application needs in sports, this review summarizes emerging applications of wearable sensing technologies enabled by conductive composites and AI. First, the relevance to sports science and the data characteristics of physiological, biochemical, and biomechanical signals are introduced. The functional characteristics, representative applications, and major limitations of conductive polymer, carbon-based, MXene, and hydrogel composites are then summarized. Regarding algorithms, the fundamental principles of supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs) are discussed, with comparisons of their capabilities in feature extraction, temporal modeling, and multisource data analysis, as well as their input data requirements. On this basis, advances in the application of these systems to sports performance and sport-specific movement monitoring, exercise-induced fatigue monitoring and assessment, sports injury identification and evaluation, and intelligent monitoring of sports rehabilitation are reviewed followed by a discussion of current challenges and future directions. Through the coordinated integration of material design, signal acquisition, and intelligent analysis, wearable systems are expected to enable continuous, reliable, and individualized assessment of exercise-related states, with further applications in real-time feedback, risk alerts, and training decision support, providing a technological foundation for scientifically informed training, sports rehabilitation, and individual health management.

title: Organic Upconversion Devices for NIR–II Biometric Sensing and Imaging Enabled by an Isomerically Engineered Narrow-Bandgap Quinoidal Polymer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The limited availability of organic donor materials absorbing beyond 1000 nm fundamentally limits the development of solution-processed photodetectors and upconversion devices (UCDs) in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window. Herein, we report DPP-TbT, a narrow-bandgap alternating copolymer realized through isomeric engineering of the thiophene backbone. By employing a thieno[3,4-b]thiophene (TbT) quinoidal donor fused to a diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) acceptor, the absorption onset is extended to ∼1300 nm, enabling intrinsic NIR-II photon harvesting. When blended with the benchmark non-fullerene acceptor Y6 to form bulk-heterojunction photodetectors, the DPP-TbT:Y6 system achieves a specific detectivity exceeding 1011 Jones at 1064 nm with a linear dynamic range (LDR) of 68 dB. Monolithic integration of this photodetector with a quantum-dot light-emitting diode further yields a UCD that directly transduces 1064 nm excitation into visible emission with a turn-on voltage of ∼2 V, a luminance of 3741 cd m–2, and a luminance-LDR of 60 dB. We further demonstrate real-time heart-rate monitoring via photoplethysmography, high-resolution biological imaging (5080 ppi), and visualization of hidden information through a 1000 nm long-pass filter. This work establishes isomeric engineering as a rational strategy for accessing ultra-narrow bandgaps and advancing low-cost, wearable NIR-II visualization and biometric sensing systems.

title: High-Performance Planar Ni/Si Photothermoelectric Photodetectors Enabled by MnO2 Nanosheets
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photodetectors are the key component of modern communication systems, surveillance applications, robotics, and scientific research. The photothermoelectric effect offers opportunity to fabricate broadband and self-driven photodetectors utilizing thermally energized charge carriers. Unfortunately, photothermoelectric photodetectors are facing the challenge of large dark current, leading to low detectivity, linear dynamic range, and on–off ratio. Herein, we design a planar Ni/n-Si device structure with the help of a monolayer of MnO2 nanosheets for contact engineering. The demonstrated device shows a broadband detection range from 200 nm to MIR with an external quantum efficiency of 263.6%, a photoresponsivity of 455.1 mA W–1, a detectivity of ∼7.25 × 1012 Jones, and an on–off ratio of ∼103 at 0 V. Additionally, the device shows an unprecedented bias-assisted photoresponsivity and external quantum efficiency of 21.56 A W–1 and 13,363%, respectively, with 200 nm illumination at –10 V. The nanosheet-based contact engineering provides a powerful strategy to fabricate self-powered photodetectors with high photoresponsivity, external quantum efficiency, and broadband detection from the solar blind region to the MIR spectrum.

title: Interface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Sensor Enabled by Hairy-Particle-Analyte Noncovalent Coupling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Raman enhancement in practical sensing is dominated by surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), where signal amplification relies on localized plasmonic hotspots but is often limited by inefficient analyte access. Conventional SERS platforms further require multistep assembly on rigid substrates, exhibit ligand-limited stability associated with thiol-metal coordination, and rely on time-consuming off-site detection (>12 h), limiting reproducibility and practical deployment. Here, we develop an interface-engineered SERS strategy, referred to as interface-enhanced Raman scattering (IERS), in which a polymer-grafted plasmonic interface regulates analyte enrichment and access to electromagnetic hotspots. Diblock copolymer-grafted gold nanoparticles form “hairy” particles, in which an N-heterocyclic carbene-functionalized block drives spontaneous interparticle hotspot formation, while a poly(acrylic acid) block promotes noncovalent analyte enrichment and nanoconfinement. This interfacial nanoconfinement suppresses fluorescence and is consistent with an additional charge-transfer contribution. As a result, IERS enables rapid fabrication via simple mixing of “hairy” particles in soft hydrogels, robust stability through multidentate NHC coordination, and fast on-site detection (<15 min). The sensor achieves broadband trace detection, strong tolerance to fluorescent interference, and excellent batch-to-batch reproducibility. The conformal sensing capability was further demonstrated by proof-of-concept detection of prothioconazole on a pesticide-spiked curved apple surface.

title: Organic Spacer Cation Engineering Enhances the Electroluminescence of Full-Color PeLEDs
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites have great potential in pure-blue perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs). Nevertheless, disordered multi-n phase distribution gives rise to inhomogeneous quantum confinement, accompanied by high charge-transport barriers, which severely restrict the performance of pure-blue devices. This paper proposes a universal dual-functional modification strategy, which achieves efficient pure-blue PeLEDs by partially replacing phenethylammonium bromide (PEABr) with 2-methoxyethylammonium bromide (MOAmBr). Due to the smaller steric hindrance of MOAmBr and its strong interaction with the perovskite framework, it can effectively reduce the interlayer spacing of quasi-2D perovskites and regulate the distribution of phases, thereby enhancing quantum confinement and achieving a blueshift and high-purity electroluminescence (EL). At the same time, MOAmBr reduces the carrier injection barrier, improves charge migration, and inhibits internal recombination losses of the device. The optimized pure-blue PeLED achieves a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 6.8% at 469 nm. Additionally, this universal strategy is successfully applied to green and red PeLEDs, achieving significant EQE values of 21.69 and 17.29% at 506 and 660 nm, respectively. This work provides a simple and versatile cation engineering method for constructing high-performance full-spectrum quasi-2D PeLEDs.

title: Polarized 3D Bicontinuous bcu Covalent Organic Frameworks with Accessible Octa-Sites for High-Efficiency Oxygen Electrocatalysis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional (3D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are potential metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) due to their inherent porosity and potential for fully exposed active sites. However, their practical application is severely hindered by inefficient electron transport along the extended framework and the resultant high kinetic barriers. Herein, we report a series of highly crystalline and non-interpenetrated 8-connected body-centered cubic (bcu) COFs featuring eight unstacked catalytic nodes per unit cell for ORR. By integrating redox-active azobenzene (Azo) units into the linkages, we successfully bridge the gap between electronic conductivity and catalytic activity. The incorporated Azo moieties not only narrow the bandgap but also serve as electron reservoirs, facilitating rapid electron shuttling to the imine-based active sites. Consequently, the optimal DZPy-COF achieves a remarkable half-wave potential of 0.77 V under alkaline conditions, coupled with a high turnover frequency (0.03 s–1) and enhanced capacitance (13.7 mF cm–2). Theoretical calculations reveal that the Azo units polarize the framework, lowering the energy barrier for intermediate formation, which is the rate-determining step in conventional 3D COFs. This work underscores the efficacy of leveraging high-valency topologies combined with redox-active linkages to overcome electron transport limitations in crystalline porous catalysts.

title: Sequence-Engineered Multifunctional Peptide Nanozyme Gel for Catalytic Microenvironment Regulation in Diabetic Infected Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent infection, redox imbalance, and dysregulated enzymatic activity, yet current biomaterials largely function as passive dressings, with limited capacity to actively intervene in the stalled healing cascade. Here, we report a sequence-programmed peptide nanozyme that encodes multiple enzyme-mimetic activities within a single supramolecular framework for adaptive microenvironment regulation. By mimicking the coordination motifs of natural hydrolases and superoxide dismutase, a de novo peptide sequence, C7-RD(S)HHEEH, was rationally engineered to encode integrated nitrogen/oxygen metal-binding sites. The incorporation of a side-chain–modified serine enhances coordination adaptability, while glutamate residues facilitate catalytic functionality. Upon Cu2+ coordination, the peptide self-assembles into a nanozyme exhibiting hydrolase (HYD)-, oxidase (OXD)-, peroxidase (POD)-, and superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activities within a unified framework, thereby enabling coordinated regulation of enzymatic debridement, antibacterial defense, and redox homeostasis. Incorporated into a sprayable gelatin hydrogel, the nanozyme provides conformal wound coverage while maintaining excellent biocompatibility and sustained catalytic functionality. In a diabetic bacteria-infected wound model, the nanozyme gel significantly accelerates wound closure, enhances angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and restores tissue regeneration. Our work demonstrates that rational peptide sequence design can encode complex, multimodal catalysis into synthetic nanozymes, offering a programmable approach for active regulation of pathological microenvironments in chronic wound therapy.

title: Structural Reconstruction of Ternary CuCo2S4 for Boosting Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a promising strategy for sustainable ammonia synthesis while simultaneously addressing nitrate pollution in wastewater. However, the irreversible structural reconstruction commonly observed in catalysts during NO3RR obscures the true active sites and complicates mechanistic understanding. In this study, flower-like CuCo2S4 nanocrystals synthesized via a hot-injection method serve as a model ternary sulfide system to systematically probe reconstruction dynamics and identify active phases under operating conditions. Experimental characterizations reveal that CuCo2S4 gradually evolves into Cu-Co(OH)2/Co9S8 through electrochemical reconstruction. This reconstructed catalyst exhibits excellent NO3RR performance, achieving an average Faradaic efficiency of 97.3%, an ammonia production rate of 363.1 μmol h–1 mg–1, and remarkable cycling stability. In situ FTIR spectra indicate that Cu incorporation promotes the conversion of *NO2 and accelerates subsequent hydrogenation steps. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that Cu doping facilitates *NH3 desorption and optimizes the balance between NO3– adsorption and *NH3 release. This work systematically deciphers the reconstruction pathway of sulfide catalysts during NO3RR, offering fundamental insights into electrocatalyst reconstruction mechanisms and providing a design strategy for high-performance ammonia-production electrocatalysts.

title: Ag Nanowire/Mo2CTx Transparent Electrodes with Chemically Tunable Work Function for Near- and Shortwave-Infrared Photodetectors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transparent electrodes that simultaneously combine low sheet resistance, broadband infrared transparency, and tunable interfacial energetics are critically needed for emerging infrared optoelectronics, yet are rarely achieved within a single solution-processable architecture. Here, we report a hybrid transparent electrode composed of a percolative Ag nanowire network overcoated with Mo2CTx MXene nanosheets (Ag/MX). In this architecture, Ag nanowires provide an efficient conductive scaffold, while the Mo2CTx overlayer bridges interwire junctions, smooths the surface, and governs the device-facing interfacial electronic structure. The resulting electrodes exhibit a low sheet resistance of 18.84 Ω/sq together with a transmittance of 82% at 1550 nm and an average transmittance of 80.84% over 1500–2500 nm. More importantly, two distinct surface-modification routes enable chemically tunable work-function states: polyethyleneimine lowers the work function through interfacial dipole formation, whereas UV/Ozone treatment raises it through oxygen-enriched surface termination and mild surface oxidation of the Mo2CTx overlayer. These chemically distinct low and high work function states allow the common AgNW/Mo2CTx (Ag/MX) electrode architecture to meet different carrier-selective requirements in quantum dot short-wave-infrared and organic near-infrared photodetectors. This work establishes a chemically tunable transparent-electrode platform for cross-material infrared photodetection and provides a strategy for integrating infrared transparency, electrical transport, and carrier-selective interfacial energetics within a common electrode architecture.

title: Enhancing feasibility of cost-optimal energy systems in surrogate-assisted design optimization
abstract: Energy system design optimization often incurs high computational cost, which limits applications such as uncertainty analysis and interactive decision support. Surrogate models reduce this cost by emulating expensive original models. In surrogate-assisted design optimization (SADO), an upper-level optimization algorithm searches over designs while surrogate models emulate operational optimizations to evaluate each design. Existing SADO studies rarely enforce feasibility, defined here as the ability of an energy system to satisfy all demand constraints.This study quantifies how the choice of a feasibility predictor influences the cost and feasibility of designs obtained from SADO applied to a convex energy system model. We compare three feasibility predictors: two artificial neural networks and a convex hull predictor that classifies feasibility by membership in a feasible input space. We embed each predictor into SADO and evaluate predicted designs by their cost and feasibility when re-evaluated in the operational optimization.The results show that the feasibility predictor strongly affects both cost and feasibility of designs. SADO with neural-network-based feasibility predictors achieves feasible designs consistently only if oversizing is enforced. In contrast, SADO with the convex hull predictor yields guaranteed feasible designs by construction and produces designs whose objective values are typically within 2 % of the cost-optimal solution. This improved feasibility comes at the expense of increased computational cost compared to neural-network-based feasibility predictors. Overall, these results establish feasibility prediction as a critical design choice in SADO and identify geometric feasibility predictors as robust alternatives to data-driven surrogate models for convex energy system models.

title: Interfacial Polymerization Using Acyl Chloride-Functionalized Porphyrin Comonomers toward Robust PA-66 with Type I/II Dual Photodynamic Antibacterial Durability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The growing threat of bacterial contamination and antibiotic resistance urgently requires functional antibacterial textiles. Photodynamic antibacterial approaches relying on reactive oxygen species (ROS) provide a promising alternative to achieve safe and long-term antimicrobial protection. Herein, a fabrication strategy was developed to construct intrinsically photodynamic antibacterial polyamide 66 (PA-66) yarns via interfacial polymerization. Acyl chloride-modified porphyrin (TCPP-Cl4), acting as a ternary monomer, was covalently grafted onto PA-66 molecular chains via interfacial polymerization. Subsequent drawing, spinning, and twisting yielded functional TCPP-Cl4-PA-66 yarns that preserved the favorable mechanical performance and thermal stability of PA-66. Physically blended TCPP/PA-66 yarns were also prepared as reference samples. Compared with TCPP/PA-66 yarns, the covalent anchoring process effectively reduced photosensitizer leaching and improved ROS generation capacity. As a result, TCPP-Cl4-PA-66 yarns achieved antibacterial efficiencies of 97.4 ± 1.3% against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and 94.0 ± 2.8% against Escherichia coli (E. coli). Furthermore, this covalent immobilization also endowed the yarns with favorable washing resistance, maintaining stable photodynamic antibacterial activity against both strains after multiple washing cycles. Interwoven fabrics fabricated from TCPP/PA-66, TCPP-Cl4-PA-66, and cotton yarns also exhibited desirable photodynamic antibacterial performance. This work provides a facile strategy for constructing photodynamic antibacterial textile materials with good stability.

title: Structural and Esaki-Diode-like Electrical Properties of PLD-Grown 2D MoS2 Film on MBE Grown AlN/Si(111) Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract MoS2 thin films were synthesized via pulsed laser deposition (PLD) onto AlN/Si(111) templates, where the AlN buffer layers (110 and 200 nm thick) were grown by molecular beam epitaxy. We achieved excellent MoS2 thickness uniformity (≈3 monolayers) and confirmed the conformal coverage of the PLD-grown films by Raman mapping. Transmission electron microscopy analysis confirmed the epitaxial character of the AlN film and the presence of an ultrathin aluminum oxynitride layer on its surface. Following X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis, oxygen impurities were confirmed in the bulk AlN film as well. Heterojunctions between the ultrathin MoS2 film and AlN, investigated by current–voltage characterization of vertical diode structures, exhibit Esaki-diode-like behavior with a negative-resistance zone. A diagram of the energy bands and Fermi levels in the heterostructure composed of the thick oxygen-doped AlN film sandwiched between the MoS2 and Si electrodes was proposed, and the observed Esaki-diode-like current–voltage characteristic was attributed to electron tunneling from the oxygen impurity band in the AlN film into the valence band of the degenerate p-MoS2 film.

title: Nanofiber Density Is a Higher-Order Architectural Regulator of Multidimensional Cardiomyocyte Maturation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Insufficient maturation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) remains a major challenge in cardiac tissue engineering. While electrospun nanofibers offer biomimetic topographical and mechanical cues, conventional high-density fiber architectures impose excessive mechanical constraints that restrict mechanotransduction and limit CM maturation. Here, we employed a suspended, aligned electrospun polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofiber platform to investigate how fiber density—categorized as low (LD; 15.89 ± 1.84 μg/cm2), medium (MD; 85.81 ± 12.74 μg/cm2), and high (HD; 404.90 ± 59.10 μg/cm2)—modulates the maturation of neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (NRCMs). The MD substrate was identified as the optimal configuration, effectively balancing topographical guidance with a permissive mechanical microenvironment for NRCM maturation. Compared with the HD substrate, NRCMs on MD substrates exhibited enhanced structural maturation, with a greater aspect ratio (5.65 ± 1.15) and sarcomere length (1.92 ± 0.17 μm). These structural improvements were accompanied by enhanced gap junction formation and improved electromechanical function, including a 4.03-fold higher contraction displacement and a 4.01-fold faster calcium decay rate. Furthermore, the MD substrate promoted metabolic maturation, evidenced by a 2.08-fold increase in mitochondrial membrane potential and a 2.42-fold higher ATP production. The LD substrate exhibited an intermediate maturation phenotype between MD and HD groups. Mechanistically, the maturation-promoting effects of the MD substrate were associated with increased YAP phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention, together with enhanced PI3K–Akt signaling, all of which were attenuated by high-density fiber packing. This "Goldilocks effect" establishes fiber density as a critical architectural determinant of CM maturation and highlights optimization of this parameter to regulate mechanosignaling as an effective strategy for engineering functionally mature cardiomyocytes.

title: Integration of Charged Peptide Amphiphiles within Lipid Nanoparticles (LNPs) for Enhanced Targeted mRNA Delivery
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) play a pivotal role in mRNA-based therapy; however, achieving targeted delivery remains challenging. We developed an LNP platform integrating peptide amphiphiles (PAs) to exploit their dual bioactivity and electrostatic tunability. Two PAs, cationic C16TAT (derived from a cell-penetrating peptide) and anionic C16HA2 (based on an endosomolytic peptide), were co-assembled into LNPs. In vitro, C16TAT/LNPs significantly enhanced mRNA delivery across multiple cell lines via improved cellular uptake. Due to the potent charge-modifying capacity of C16HA2, C16HA2/LNPs exhibit spleen-selective tropism in vivo, achieving >100-fold higher mRNA expression in the spleen than in the liver. While the commonly used surface-conjugated TAT-PEG-LNPs enhanced transfection in vitro, their in vivo performance was inferior relative to the C16TAT/LNP system due to the lack of stability, highlighting the advantage of PA integration. Critically, effective tissue targeting required substantial LNP charge alteration (pKa and zeta potential), which was achievable with C16HA2 but not C16TAT, likely due to the former’s higher aggregation tendency. Dual PA-PEG modifications may improve spleen targeting but required formulation optimization. This work establishes a simple PA/lipid co-assembly approach as a robust method for modulating LNP tropism, advancing the rational design of targeted mRNA delivery systems.

title: Inhibition of Oxidative Activity by Photo-induced Surface Hydroxyl Groups in Bismuth Titanium Oxide Photocatalysts Detected by Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The surface structure of semiconductor photocatalysts plays a critical role in the extraction of charge carriers during photocatalytic reactions. However, the surface structures of many photocatalysts are dynamic under catalytic conditions, which makes identifying photo-induced changes and their effect on photocatalytic activity challenging. Herein, we use super-resolution, single-molecule fluorescence imaging to map the spatial distribution of catalytically active regions and quantify the changes in activity of those regions for photocatalytic oxidation in bismuth titanium oxide (Bi4Ti3O12) nanoplates. Individual nanoplates varied widely in both activity and stability, reflecting significant heterogeneity among a single synthesis batch of photocatalyst particles. We observed that while the nanoplates are more active around the perimeter of the basal facet, those perimeter regions decrease in activity at the same relative rate as the rest of the basal facet, indicating a spatially uniform degradation mechanism. Through ensemble structural characterization of the nanoplates after irradiation, we identified surface hydroxyl groups as the photo-induced feature. Our results indicate that surface hydroxyl groups introduce hole trap states that increase charge recombination at the surface of the nanoplates, leading to the observed decrease in activity. Surprisingly, we identified nanoscale features that do not begin with high activity but exhibit a slower rate of activity loss, leading to regions with greater activity relative to the rest of the basal facet at the end of imaging. Our findings highlight the importance of not only understanding how different nanoscale features influence catalytic activity but also how these features evolve over time, which dictates catalyst stability.

title: Flexible and Bridge-Free CuI Mutual Capacitive Arrays for Machine Learning-Assisted Three-Dimensional Spatial Interactive Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible transparent human–machine interfaces (HMIs) are fundamentally bottlenecked by the brittleness of conventional indium tin oxide (ITO), the mechanical vulnerability of photolithographic bridged structures, and the complex hardware shielding required to suppress capacitive crosstalk. Herein, we propose a hardware-algorithm co-design strategy featuring a bridge-free double-sided (BFDS) mutual capacitive sensor array based on magnetron-sputtered p-type γ-CuI thin films. By employing a simplified floating-electrode readout scheme, the transparent flexible array not only captures high-fidelity two-dimensional (2D) tactile signals (signal-to-noise ratio of 268.5 ± 5.6) but also unlocks highly sensitive three-dimensional (3D) proximity perception (0–5 cm) driven by fringing electric fields. To overcome the global spatial crosstalk intrinsically induced by the unshielded hardware, a customized lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is integrated. The CNN robustly decodes the complex nonlinear capacitance matrices, achieving an overall test accuracy of 86.2%. Furthermore, the CuI/PET structure exhibits good robustness over 10,000 extreme bending cycles (radius of 2.5 mm), where the grain-boundary scattering serves as a strain-release mechanism while preserving a continuous percolating conductive network. This work demonstrates that algorithmic compensation can relax stringent hardware shielding constraints, paving a novel avenue for ultra-simplified, touchless, and intelligent wearable electronics.

title: Interface-Engineered Electrochemical CO2 Reduction to Formate Coupled with Enzymatic Dihydroxyacetone Production
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract While the electroreduction of CO2 to high-value chemicals provides a revolutionary strategy for achieving sustainable development, the direct synthesis of multi-carbon products remains a prominent challenge. Herein, an integrated strategy that combines renewable electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reactions (eCO2RR) with enzyme cascades for the high-value-added production of dihydroxyacetone is proposed. Specifically, bismuth nanocatalysts were doped with sulfur to modulate the surface electronic structure, leading to the significantly accelerated formation of *HCOO intermediates. Consequently, a 94.7% formate Faradaic efficiency was attained at 300 mA cm–2, and good long-term catalytic stability was achieved. Moreover, a 4 cm2 membrane electrode electrolyzer was employed with a 0.1 M KHCO3 neutral electrolyte to concentrate the formate product and protect the downstream enzymes from the alkaline electrolyte. The cofactor NADH was directly regenerated using a copper foam electrode, driving an enzymatic cascade to convert formate to 2.77 g L–1 dihydroxyacetone without external carbon supplementation. This work presents a DHA synthesis method, which is solely electricity-driven and involves the direct reaction of CO2 and H2O, without requiring any externally supplied cofactors or stoichiometric reductants. By exploiting the fine selectivity and efficiency of enzyme catalysis, this formate-mediated pathway maximizes carbon utilization and significantly expands the chemical space accessible to carbon dioxide.

title: Ion-Conductive Elastomers with Enhanced Mechanical Performance and Electrical Conductivity via a Nano-Synergistic Transport Mechanism
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible ion-conductive elastomers have emerged as promising materials for wearable humidity sensors owing to their excellent stretchability and efficient ion transport capability. However, simultaneously achieving high ionic conductivity and excellent mechanical performance remains a significant challenge, primarily because the incorporation of high loadings of ionic components often induces solvation effects within polymer networks and compromises their mechanical stability. To address this challenge, we developed an ion-conductive elastomer with enhanced mechanical robustness and efficient ion transport capability by constructing a hydrogen-bond-anchored micro/nanostructured conductive network. Specifically, amino-functionalized SiO2 serves not only as a nanoreinforcing phase but also as a “bridging node” for ion transport through multiple hydrogen-bond anchoring interactions with polyurethane chains, enabling the formation of a continuous micro/nanoscale ionic conductive network while preserving the structural stability of the polymer matrix. The resulting ion-conductive elastomer exhibits high ionic conductivity (1.4 × 10–2 S/m), high tensile strength (2.17 MPa), and recyclability, achieving an effective synergy between mechanical performance and ion transport properties. Based on a humidity-induced ion transport mechanism, the fabricated flexible humidity sensor demonstrates rapid, stable, and reversible responses over a broad relative humidity range. This work provides a new material design strategy for developing high-performance, sustainable, and flexible ion-conductive polyurethane-based wearable humidity sensors.

title: Microfluidic Production of Mangiferin-Loaded Liposomes Enables Gut–Joint Axis Modulation for Early Osteoarthritis Intervention
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microfluidic nanomanufacturing provides a controllable and scalable strategy for improving the oral delivery of poorly bioavailable natural compounds. Herein, mangiferin-loaded liposomes (Lip@MG) were fabricated using an in-house-developed continuous microfluidic platform integrated with a high-efficiency micromixer and evaluated as a gut–joint axis-oriented intervention for early knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Compared with the conventional batch method, microfluidic synthesis produced Lip@MG with a more uniform spherical morphology, a clearly defined bilayer structure, and a narrower particle size distribution. By adjusting the flow-rate ratio, Lip@MG with tunable particle sizes from 207.8 to 118.6 nm, reduced polydispersity, and stable negative zeta potentials of up to approximately –35 mV was obtained. In vitro, Lip@MG exhibited favorable cytocompatibility and enhanced chondrocyte viability. Transcriptomic analysis, qRT-PCR, and western blot further indicated that Lip@MG attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in chondrocytes, at least partly by suppressing NF-κB signaling and inhibiting p65 phosphorylation. In an anterior cruciate ligament transection-induced KOA mouse model, oral Lip@MG administration alleviated cartilage degeneration, increased cartilage thickness from 132 to 215 μm, reduced the OARSI score from 2.5 to 1.5, increased subchondral bone mineral density by 27%, and restored colonic barrier integrity, as reflected by a 65% reduction in the colonic histopathological score. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing revealed that Lip@MG reshaped KOA-associated gut dysbiosis by partially restoring the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes balance and enriching potentially beneficial taxa. These findings demonstrate that microfluidically manufactured Lip@MG is a promising nutritional nanocarrier for microbiota-centered early KOA intervention through coordinated regulation of intestinal homeostasis and joint degeneration.

title: Atomic Resolution Microscopy Reveals Cluster, Charge Transport, and Diffusion Metrics in Guest:Host Blend Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quantitatively determining the 3D arrangement of guest molecules in a guest:host emissive layer remains a challenge, particularly for beam-sensitive organic materials. By extracting 3D coordinates from depth-sectioned HAADF–STEM stacks of Ir(ppy)2(acac):TCTA and Ir(ppy)3:TCTA vacuum-deposited guest:host blend films, we enable direct access to molecular-scale morphology in beam-sensitive materials. We find that guest aggregation is significantly stronger than expected from random distributions, with the difference diminishing only at high concentrations. Coupling these morphologies to master equation transport modeling reveals that aggregation alters transport pathways and reduces mobility. Additionally, thermal motion of guest molecules between the image frames provides an estimate of molecular diffusion, linking structural and dynamic behavior.

title: A Graphene Oxide-Based Tribo-Piezoelectric Hybrid Sensor for Armed Swimming Action Recognition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Limb movement analysis provides a convenient and effective approach for physiological safety monitoring and motion standardization assessment of personnel working in humid, wading, or underwater environments. However, in wet and wading environments, the existing wearable flexible sensors generally suffer from several limitations such as insufficient sensitivity, rapid performance degradation, and poor environmental stability. In this paper, we propose a corrosion-resistant tribo-piezoelectric hybrid sensor (CRTPHS) primarily composed of an intrinsically corrosion-resistant fluorinated graphene oxide film with a micro-truncated pyramid array structure (MFGOF) and gold-coated polydimethylsiloxane-barium zirconate titanate (PDMS-BZT). The CRTPHS exhibited a sensitivity of up to 1.86 V/N, a response time of 106 ms, a peak power density of 1.98 mW/m2, and stable output performance after 50,000 cycles. In corrosion resistance tests, the CRTPHS retained a sensitivity of 1.27 V/N and excellent underwater sensing capability even after 3 days of seawater immersion. By integrating a lightweight random forest (RF) algorithm, the CRTPHS enabled recognition of five simulated armed-swimming motion states, achieving an average cross-subject accuracy of 99.25% ± 0.07% under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV). This study not only provides a novel fabrication method for developing corrosion-resistant self-powered sensors but also offers a new strategy for intelligent posture recognition in corrosive seawater environments.

title: Chemically Active Interfaces Enable Modular Manufacturing of DLP 3D Printed Hydrogel Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydrogel-based flexible sensors are promising for wearable electronics, while digital light processing (DLP) printing enables customized device fabrication. However, DLP manufacturing remains largely limited to monolithic structures because freshly printed hydrogels lack sufficient mechanical stability for constructing curved or enclosed architectures. Here, a modular manufacturing strategy is developed by enabling post-printing polymerization through a sustained radical-generation system comprising Cu2+, lignosulfonate (LS), and ammonium persulfate (APS). Unlike conventional photoinitiated systems that become inactive after light exposure, the Cu2+–LS complex maintains a dynamic Cu2+/Cu+ redox cycle in the dark, continuously activating APS to generate radicals. Consequently, independently printed hydrogel modules undergo interfacial polymerization and reconstruct a continuous covalent network, enabling assembled hydrogels to exhibit bulk-like load-bearing performance with failure occurring outside the assembled interface. The Cu–LS system also introduces mobile ions, imparting intrinsic ionic conductivity for strain sensing without conductive fillers. Using this approach, ring-integrated and kirigami-patterned wearable sensors are fabricated through modular assembly. A fingertip-mounted device achieves 99% accuracy in classifying ten sign-language gestures and enables real-time intelligent wheelchair control. This work converts hydrogel interfaces from inactive boundaries into active reconstruction sites, offering a versatile route to the modular fabrication of mechanically integrated soft electronics.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Despite being deployed in various stationary and transportation applications, the limited durability and reliability hinder their full commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in some particular cases. This review systematically discusses EIS’s implementation, interpretation, and application for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measuring time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and model-free interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these results, the application of EIS to performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics is discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide the EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review offers comprehensive perspectives on the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells, providing valuable insights for academic researchers and industry practitioners in addressing the durability and reliability challenges.

title: Single- and few-layer materials: synthesis, structure–property relationships, integration of AI/ML, and energy storage applications
Control of spin-to-charge conversion by chirality switching of spin texture in a three-dimensional hybrid perovskite
abstract: A strategy to switch the chirality of spin texture in hybrid perovskites, without the aid of an applied electric field, has been established. The switching of spin texture chirality can be used to manipulate the spin-to-charge conversion. The electric current, generated by coherent magnon mediated spin current or photo induced spin current, changes sign during the transition from static to dynamic Rashba effect, which demonstrates its applications in spintronic and magnonic devices.

title: Secondary materials in photovoltaics manufacturing
abstract: The use of secondary materials in photovoltaics could reduce resource demand, waste generation and supply-chain risks. This Review benchmarks recycled content use across silicon photovoltaic materials and identifies technical and market barriers to wider adoption.

title: Set efficiency criteria for access to geological carbon dioxide storage
abstract: Geological CO2 storage sites are critical to achieving climate-relevant carbon sequestration. Efficiency metrics should be used to ensure that limited storage capacity is not used on CO2 from capture projects with high levels of life-cycle carbon emissions.

title: Role of Dynamics and Spin-State Crossover in Metal-Hydride Hydrogen Atom Transfer (MHAT) and Electron Transfer in Transmetalation during Co–Ni Multimetallic Catalyzed Alkene Hydroarylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal-hydride hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT) reactions involve hydrogen transfer from a transition-metal hydride to an alkene to generate a metal radical and carbon-centered radical pair. These radicals can then either collapse to a metal–alkyl intermediate or separate into solvent-separated radicals. Little is currently known about the factors that control the lifetime of MHAT-generated radical pairs and subsequent reaction pathway selectivity. Therefore, we used density functional theory calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics trajectories with explicit solvent to evaluate the Co-hydride (Co–H) MHAT reaction in the Co/Ni dual-catalyzed alkene hydroarylation transformation. The trajectories showed that ultrafast dynamic effects combined with singlet-to-triplet spin-state crossover determine whether there is a fast collapse to the Co-alkyl intermediate or a longer-lived solvent-caged radical pair intermediate. Calculations also demonstrated that the Co-alkyl intermediate generated from the MHAT reaction can interface with the Ni catalytic cycle through a combined electron-transfer/alkyl-group-transfer mechanism. Overall, these time-resolved mechanistic details provide insight into the Co–H MHAT reaction process and how Co catalysis is integrated with Ni catalysis.

title: Topology-Directed Pore Space Compartmentalization and Densification in MOFs Enable Record Trace C3H6 Capture and C2H4 Purification
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive separation of C3H6 from C2H4 is of great relevance yet highly challenging to the petrochemical industry, especially for trace C3H6 capture. Here, we constructed two metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), NKU-410 and NKU-411, through pillaring of the kgd- and hxl-topology supermolecular building layers (SBLs) comprised of a novel fluoride-bridging hexanuclear niccolite cluster. In terms of topological net merging and pillaring, a three-dimensional compartmentalization of pore space was implemented, reconstructing the less confined pore space in NKU-410 into a dense array of uniform strongly confined pore cavities in NKU-411. Leveraging the pore confinement effect, NKU-411 impressively attains an ultrahigh C3H6 uptake of 47.5 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 0.01 bar, together with an appreciable C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) selectivity of 36.9, placing it among the benchmark MOFs for trace C3H6 capture from C2H4. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrated that NKU-411 shows excellent C2H4 purification and C3H6 recovery performances at ambient conditions over a wide range of separation scenarios with varying feed concentrations and compositions, remarkably affording a record-breaking C2H4 (≥99.999% pure) productivity of 639.4 L kg–1 from C3H6/C2H4 (1/99, v/v) mixture. In-depth mechanistic studies disclosed that the well-tailored pore cavity in NKU-411 represents a “sweet spot” for C3H6 and the dense arrangement of such “sweet spot” maximally optimizes the pore space utilization, providing a new paradigm for boosting the ultralow-pressure gas adsorption capacity and selectivity for MOFs.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Control Enables Regulated Growth of Functional Metal–Phenolic Network Films
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–phenolic network (MPN) films are of widespread interest because of their potential application in biotechnology, catalysis, and the environment. Their formation typically involves the supramolecular assembly of phenolic ligands and metal ions from solution onto a solid substrate. Such assembly has been conducted exclusively from a single-phase solution, thus limiting spatiotemporal control over coordination and/or the range of precursors that can be used, and thereby restricting the compositional and structural diversity, as well as functionality, of MPN films. Herein, we report a liquid–liquid interfacial assembly (LLIA) approach, which leverages two immiscible phases, to prepare functional MPN films with specific properties. LLIA enables both the kinetic regulation of film growth (a key parameter in designing films with desired properties) and the use of a broader range of building blocks. The assembled MPN films exhibit controlled thickness (∼30–500 nm) and stiffness (∼2–12 GPa) and distinct structural properties (e.g., crystallinity) relative to other methods, which contribute to their conductivity and molecular selectivity (e.g., H2/CO2 separation performance). Functional MPN films with wettability, conductivity, antibacterial, or fluorescence properties are assembled by integrating various functional components (e.g., polymers, nanoparticles, and dyes), as well as inorganic and metal–organic framework films.

title: Optimizing systems rather than parts
abstract: Developing and deploying clean technologies to reach net-zero carbon emissions will require more than optimizing individual processes and technologies. System-level thinking is needed to identify trade-offs, handle uncertainty and future scenarios, and support decision-making, as highlighted by articles in a new Collection.

Diffusion-Gating Enabled Ternary C2H4 Purification and Inverse C2H2/CO2 Separation in an Adaptive Hopf-Link Metal–Organic Framework
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous purification of polymer-grade ethylene (C2H4) and recovery of high-purity acetylene (C2H2) from complex ternary mixtures with carbon dioxide (CO2) represents a critical industrial challenge. Conventional adsorbents employ thermodynamic selectivity to bind C2H2 and CO2 preferentially over C2H4, enabling one-step C2H4 purification but necessitating an energy-intensive desorption step for C2H2 recovery, as C2H2 typically binds more strongly. Here, we report a fundamentally different approach using diffusion-gating in an adaptive Hopf-link metal–organic framework, ZJNU-600, which replaces thermodynamic control. The framework comprises two orthogonal, interpenetrated sql nets mechanically interlocked as Hopf links, with thiocyanate linkers acting as molecular hinges that modulate the pore aperture. This architecture establishes an ideal kinetic diffusion hierarchy of CO2 > C2H2 > C2H4, completely inverting the elution order compared to equilibrium-based separation. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that ZJNU-600 achieves one-step production of C2H4 from ternary mixtures while simultaneously enabling the direct recovery of C2H2 via inverse separation, eliminating the need for energy-intensive desorption. The exceptionally low isosteric heat of CO2 adsorption (24.7 kJ mol–1) further suggests minimal regeneration energy. Computational studies reveal that the diffusion barrier hierarchy arises from the differential chemical compatibility of each gas with the hydroxyl-decorated pore walls. This work establishes kinetic pore-aperture engineering as a generalizable and energy-efficient design principle for multicomponent gas separations, effectively inverting the separation hierarchy dictated by thermodynamic affinity.

title: Interfacial Anion Activation for Durable Aqueous Zn-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Designing a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is pivotal for stabilizing the Zn anode/electrolyte interface in aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, the mechanism of SEI formation in AZIBs remains insufficiently understood, particularly when additives induce the formation of mixed inorganic and organic SEI components during electrochemical reactions. Herein, we demonstrate how an allylurea additive induces the formation of an organic-inorganic hybrid SEI (h-SEI) at the Zn anode interface in a ZnSO4-based electrolyte and ultimately leads to the improvement in long-term interfacial stability. Unlike conventional electrolyte designs based on contact ion-pair solvation formation, allylurea reconstructs the interfacial environment to establish an anion-rich, water-deficient region near the Zn surface, thereby promoting electric-field-driven reductive transformation of anions. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations indicate that the electrochemical activation of allylurea produces allyl cation intermediates, which mediate the stepwise conversion of sulfate anions into ZnS. The resulting ZnS-rich inorganic domains reinforce the interphase and facilitate Zn2+ transport, whereas allylurea-derived organic components enhance interfacial adhesion and mechanical compliance. Consequently, the h-SEI homogenizes Zn deposition and suppresses interfacial side reactions, enabling stable cycling of Zn||Zn symmetric cells for over 2500 h at 5 mA cm–2 and Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells for more than 10,000 cycles at 5 A g–1.

title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

title: A Device‐to‐Package Perspective on Thermal Management Materials for Electronic Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT With the continued miniaturization and integration of electronic devices, power density and local heat flux have increased substantially, making heat dissipation a major constraint on device performance and reliability. Improving thermal transport inside devices through materials engineering has therefore attracted increasing attention. In this review, we systematically summarize the thermal transport mechanisms, recent progress, and manipulation strategies of materials for thermal management of electronic devices along the internal heat‐dissipation pathway. At the device and die level, we discuss representative semiconductors, metals, and dielectrics, with emphasis on their thermal transport mechanisms and their thermal conductivity manipulation. In addition, thermal transport across microscopic interfaces is discussed. At the package level, we focus on thermal interface materials (TIMs) with emphasis on their structure–property relationships and thermal performance enhancement strategies. Across these different levels, a common principle emerges: intrinsic thermal conductivity alone is insufficient to determine the thermal performance of a material after integration, because dimensions, processing‐induced changes, and interfaces are also important. By analyzing materials along the internal heat‐dissipation pathway, this review identifies the key thermal bottlenecks and defines the material and interface requirements for a low‐resistance internal heat‐dissipation pathway in future electronic devices with high power density and a high degree of integration.

title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

title: Submolecular Selenium Enables Low‐Pressure and Recyclable All‐Solid‐State Li–Se Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐selenium (Li–Se) batteries offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their practical deployment is hindered by sluggish solid‐state redox kinetics, large volume fluctuations, and unstable solid‐solid interfaces, particularly under low stack pressure. Here we report a submolecular Se x cathode by converting crystalline cyclo‐Se 8 into amorphous single‐atom and short‐chain Se (Se x , x x @G), which increases the electronic conductivity from 6.3 × 10 −5 to 13 S cm −1 and Li + diffusivity from 1.7 × 10 −14 to 2.0 × 10 −11 cm 2 s −1 . Meanwhile, a Li 2 O‐nanoshell‐modified sulfide solid electrolyte is designed to stabilize the interface against both Li metal and Se cathode. As a result, all‐solid‐state Li–Se batteries deliver the theoretical capacity of 673 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retain 86% capacity over 2800 cycles at 3 C under 8 MPa, with stable operation down to −30°C. All‐solid‐state Li–Se pouch cells further achieve an energy density of 420 Wh kg −1 and 94% capacity retention after 300 cycles under 2.5 MPa. Post‐mortem analysis reveals that the submolecular Se x species are not only structurally preserved but also recyclable after electrochemical cycling within the solid‐state reaction environment. This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low‐pressure, recyclable, and high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS 2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS 2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS 2 . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn 2+ photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

title: Re(I)‐Based Molecular Actuator‐Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
abstract: ABSTRACT The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen‐dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor ( Re1@NMs ) that integrates a three‐dimensional rhenium(I)‐based molecular actuator ( Re1 ) with glucose oxidase (GOx)‐powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx‐catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered Re1 , screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose Y ‐axis motif undergoes E / Z photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano‐photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model, Re1@NMs ‐mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor‐infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage‐associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal‐complex‐based three‐dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor‐microenvironment‐adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

title: Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O 1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH * deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol −1 , and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm −2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm −2 . These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM 1 ‐O‐TM 2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO 4 (A 2 BO 4 ) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO 4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO 3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

title: Paradoxical effects of opioids in suppression of colonic motility
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca
                    2+
                    transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. We also found that anterogradely propagating neurogenic contractions in intact colon were suppressed by receptor-specific MOR, DOR, and KOR agonists. Together, these observations demonstrate that opioid agonists suppress inhibitory rather than excitatory motor inputs to colonic muscles. Suppression of inhibitory motor inputs precludes the precisely timed cessation of enteric inhibition that causes poststimulus depolarization and peristaltic contractions.

title: Environmental forcing, individual repeatability, and mother–daughter resemblance shape the phenology of a long-lived seabird
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli’s Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother–daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high (
                    R
                    = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother–daughter cases, daughters’ RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating into an annual fitness advantage. Differences in survival and BS across individuals were more evident during the first observed breeding attempts. Together, these results support a scenario in which plasticity shifts the population mean breeding date in response to climatic variation, while persistent traits generate differential fitness among individuals.
